## Product Overview
Sim is an open-source AI workspace platform that enables teams to build, deploy, and manage AI agents. The platform allows users to "build, deploy, and manage agents visually, conversationally, or with code" while connecting to over 1,000 integrations and major LLMs.

# Executing Deployed Sim Workflows via REST API

## Endpoint & HTTP Method

Deployed workflows are accessible at:
```
POST https://sim.ai/api/v2/workflows/{workflow-id}/execute
```

## Authentication

The platform requires an API key passed via header:
```
x-api-key: $SIM_API_KEY
```

Alternatively, workflows can be configured for public access (no authentication needed) through the "Edit API Info" modal.

## Request Body Format

Inputs are passed within an `input` object:
```json
{
  "input": { "message": "Your input here" }
}
```

The structure accommodates multiple input fields depending on your workflow's Start block configuration.

## Response Formats & Execution Modes

### Synchronous (Default)
Returns the complete result immediately:
```json
{
  "data": {
    "runId": "...",
    "output": { "result": "..." }
  }
}
```

### Streaming
Add `"stream": true` and specify `"selectedOutputs"` to receive token-by-token delivery. The documentation notes: *"Stream the response token-by-token as it is generated"*. For agent thinking/tool calls, include the header:
```
X-Sim-Stream-Protocol: agent-events-v1
```

### Asynchronous
Set `"async": true` to receive HTTP 202 with a run ID, then poll the status endpoint until completion. The platform states: *"async mode returns a run ID immediately so you don't need to hold the connection open"*.

## Rate Limits & Timeouts

Rate limits are plan-dependent and returned in response headers (`X-RateLimit-*`). Synchronous workflows have a 50-minute limit on Pro/Max/Team plans; asynchronous runs support up to 90 minutes by default, or 7 days on Enterprise with configuration.

# Sim Chat Deployment Overview

## Access & Endpoints

Chat deployments are accessed via `https://www.sim.ai/chat/your-slug` with a shareable link or embedded iframe. Programmatically, you POST to `https://www.sim.ai/api/chat/your-slug`.

## Conversation History & Sessions

Yes, Sim supports conversation continuity through an optional `conversationId` parameter. As the documentation states: "Each message triggers a new workflow execution. The full conversation history — all prior user messages and assistant responses — is passed as context so your workflow can maintain continuity across turns."

## Request/Response Format

**Request body:**
```json
{
  "input": "user message",
  "conversationId": "optional-conversation-id"
}
```

**Response:** Server-sent events (SSE) stream back in real time. Selected output fields from workflow blocks are streamed to the user.

## Authentication Options

- **Public:** No authentication
- **Password:** Shared secret in request body
- **Email:** OTP verification (6-digit code sent to allowed addresses)
- **SSO:** OIDC-based (enterprise only)

## Streaming

Responses stream back via SSE, enabling real-time text output without waiting for full execution completion.

## Key Difference from API Deployment

Chat wraps workflows in a hosted conversational UI with built-in file uploads, voice input, and access controls, requiring no application code. The standard API deployment exposes workflows as REST endpoints for programmatic integration.

<result>## Vocabulary note first

There is no "channel" concept in this codebase. The framework's term is **platform** (the type-level contract) exposed as a **provider** (the npm package that implements it). "Channel" only appears as (a) the `SPECTRUM_<CHANNEL>_<KEY>` env-var naming convention in `utils/env.ts`, and (b) fusor custom-event channel names. So a sim.ai integration = a new **provider package** implementing `definePlatform("sim_ai", …)`.

---

## 1. Monorepo layout

Bun workspaces + Turbo. Root `/Users/qwerzl/Documents/Projects/spectrum-ts/package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*", "examples/*"]`. No pnpm.

| Path | Package | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `/packages/core` | `@spectrum-ts/core` | The runtime: `Spectrum()`, content builders, fusor, `definePlatform`, authoring API |
| `/packages/spectrum-ts` | `spectrum-ts` | Batteries metapackage; re-exports core + compat shims for every provider |
| `/packages/imessage` | `@spectrum-ts/imessage` | Provider (cloud, gRPC) |
| `/packages/imessage-local` | `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local` | Provider (macOS local; explicit install, **no** `spectrum` manifest field) |
| `/packages/telegram` | `@spectrum-ts/telegram` | Provider (fusor/webhook mode) |
| `/packages/slack` | `@spectrum-ts/slack` | Provider |
| `/packages/whatsapp-business` | `@spectrum-ts/whatsapp-business` | Provider |
| `/packages/terminal` | `@spectrum-ts/terminal` | Provider (tuichat subprocess) |
| `/packages/hono`, `/express`, `/fastify`, `/elysia` | `@spectrum-ts/<framework>` | HTTP **webhook transport adapters** (not providers) |
| `/packages/test-support` | private | Shared test fixtures (`src/platform.ts`, `src/fusor.ts`, `src/webhook.ts`, `src/cloud.ts`) |
| `/examples/basic` | — | Runnable example using the terminal provider |
| `/docs` | — | `.mdx.vel` docs source |
| `/scripts/release` | — | Release tooling (auto-discovers packages) |

`turbo.json` at root declares a boundaries tag `provider` with `dependencies.deny: ["provider"]` — providers may not import each other. Each provider package has its own `turbo.json`: `{ "extends": ["//"], "tags": ["provider"] }` (e.g. `/packages/telegram/turbo.json`).

---

## 2. What a provider must implement

**Definition entry point:** `definePlatform` in `/packages/core/src/platform/define.ts` (two overloads: *regular* mode and *fusor* mode).

**The contract type:** `PlatformDef` in `/packages/core/src/platform/types.ts:275`. Its doc comment states the minimum viable integration: `name`, `config`, `lifecycle`, `user`, `space`, `messages`, `send`.

Required fields:
- `config: z.ZodType<object>` — provider config schema (line 345)
- `lifecycle.createClient(ctx: CreateClientContext)` / optional `lifecycle.destroyClient` (line 361). `CreateClientContext` (line 245) carries `{ config, projectConfig, projectId, projectSecret, store }`.
- `user.resolve({ input: { userID }, client, config, store })` (line 487), optional `user.schema`
- `space.create(...)` (line 436), optional `space.get`, `space.schema`, `space.params`, `space.actions`
- `messages: EventProducer<...>` (line 408) — **inbound**
- `send({ space, content, client, config, store }) => Promise<ProviderMessageRecord | undefined>` (line 425) — **outbound**

Optional:
- `actions?` (line 335) — two tiers: framework-recognized **platform-wise actions** `getAvatar`, `getDisplayName`, `getMembers`, `getMessage` (`PlatformWiseActions`, types.ts:93; key set `PLATFORM_WISE_ACTION_KEYS` in `/packages/core/src/platform/build.ts`), plus free-form platform-specific actions. Undeclared platform-wise actions get a default that throws `UnsupportedError`.
- `events?` (line 359) — extra streams beyond `messages` (`messages` key is reserved); surfaced flat as `spectrum.<event>` and `platform.<event>`
- `message.schema` / `message.actions` (line 369)
- `static?` — properties copied onto the returned provider callable

Key supporting types (all in `/packages/core/src/platform/types.ts`):
- `ProviderMessageRecord` (line 190) — `{ id, content, direction?, sender?, space, timestamp? } & Record<string, unknown>`; the shape both `messages` yields and `send` returns
- `ProviderUserRecord` (line 207)
- `EventProducer<TPayload, TClient, TConfig>` (line 147) — `(ctx: { client, config, projectConfig, store }) => AsyncIterable<TPayload>`
- `Platform<Def>`, `PlatformInstance<Def>`, `PlatformSpace<Def>`, `PlatformMessage<Def>`, `PlatformProviderConfig<Def>`, `PlatformRuntime`, `AnyPlatformDef` (line 502)

**Message flow:**
- *Inbound (regular mode)*: long-lived `messages` async-iterable yields `ProviderMessageRecord`s → core's `wrapProviderMessage`/`buildMessage` in `/packages/core/src/platform/build.ts` inflates them into `Message` + `PlatformSpace` → fanned out on `spectrum.messages`.
- *Inbound (fusor mode)*: `createClient` returns `fusor(platformId, verify)` (a branded `FusorClient`). Inbound arrives as a protobuf `RawInboundEvent` over a WebSocket (`/packages/core/src/fusor/websocket.ts`, default `wss://fusor-ws.spectrum.photon.codes/v1/subscribe`) or via `spectrum.webhook()`. `verify(req: FusorVerifyRequest)` authenticates + parses; `messages: FusorMessages<TPayload, TConfig>` runs once per payload and returns record(s) / `fusorEvent(channel, data)`, and may call `respond(reply)` to shape the HTTP reply. Types in `/packages/core/src/fusor/types.ts`; routing in `/packages/core/src/fusor/core.ts` (`RegisteredFusorHandler`).
- *Outbound*: everything (text, reaction, reply, typing, edit, rename, avatar, unsend, poll…) funnels through the single `send` switch on `content.type`. Sugar like `message.reply()`, `space.startTyping()` is built in `build.ts` and routes to `send`.

**Lifecycle hooks:** only `lifecycle.createClient` (required) and `lifecycle.destroyClient` (optional). Platform ID must match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$/` — enforced by `assertValidPlatformId` (define.ts:40), so use `sim_ai`, not `sim.ai` or `simAI`.

---

## 3. All existing providers / integrations

Providers (implement `definePlatform`):
- `/packages/imessage/src/index.ts` — id `imessage`, export `imessage`
- `/packages/imessage-local/src/index.ts` — id `local_imessage`, export `localIMessage`
- `/packages/telegram/src/index.ts` — id `telegram` (const `TELEGRAM_PLATFORM` in `src/config.ts`), export `telegram` — **fusor mode**
- `/packages/slack/src/index.ts` — id `slack`, export `slack`
- `/packages/whatsapp-business/src/index.ts` — id `whatsapp_business`, export `whatsappBusiness`
- `/packages/terminal/src/index.ts` — id `terminal`, export `terminal`

Not present as packages: Discord, generic webhook-as-a-provider. "Voice" is documented (`/docs/providers/voice/`) but is a SIP-level integration with no package. Slack has docs removed (commit c210674).

Webhook transport adapters (thin wrappers over `app.webhook()`, one file each):
- `/packages/hono/src/index.ts`, `/packages/express/src/index.ts`, `/packages/fastify/src/index.ts`, `/packages/elysia/src/index.ts` — all export `spectrum(options: SpectrumPluginOptions)` with `{ app, onMessage, path = "/spectrum/webhook" }`.

---

## 4. Registration & discovery

There is **no runtime plugin registry** — registration is explicit and type-driven:

1. `provider.config(cfg)` returns a `PlatformProviderConfig` tagged object (define.ts:583) carrying `__name`, `config`, `__definition`.
2. Users pass them to `Spectrum({ providers: [...] })`. Options validated by `spectrumConfigSchema` in `/packages/core/src/spectrum.ts:175`; factory options interface `SpectrumFactoryOptions` at line 262 (`providers`, `options`, `telemetry`, `webhookSecret`), `SpectrumOptions` at line 141.
3. Core keys runtimes by platform id in `spectrum.__internal.platforms` (a Map); narrowing does `spectrum.__internal.platforms.get(platformId)` (define.ts:537).

Config declaration convention: a per-provider zod schema, usually in `src/config.ts` (`/packages/telegram/src/config.ts` → `configSchema`) or `src/types.ts` (`/packages/whatsapp-business/src/types.ts:19` → `z.union([directConfig, cloudConfig])` with an `isCloudConfig` discriminator; `/packages/slack/src/types.ts` likewise).

Env fallback is automatic: `definePlatform` wraps every config schema with `envAwareConfig(platformId, def.config)` (define.ts:525), implemented in `/packages/core/src/utils/env.ts` — every string-leaf field falls back to `SPECTRUM_<PLATFORM>_<KEY>` (e.g. `SPECTRUM_SIM_AI_API_KEY`). Helpers `envFor`, `fromEnv`, `toEnvKey`, `normalizePlatformName` are re-exported from `@spectrum-ts/core/authoring`.

Discovery surfaces you'd need to touch for a new provider:
- `/packages/core/src/utils/provider-packages.ts` — `OFFICIAL_PROVIDER_PACKAGES` map (id → npm name) powering `officialProviderInstallHint` diagnostics
- `package.json#spectrum` field: `{ key, import, label }` (see `/packages/telegram/package.json`)
- `/packages/spectrum-ts/scripts/generate-manifest.ts` — builds `dist/manifest.json` by scanning `packages/*/package.json#spectrum` and **validating against source** with regex `^export\s+const\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*definePlatform\(...` in `src/index.ts`; consumed by external scaffolders like `create-spectrum-app`. `label` must equal the `definePlatform` id, `import` must equal the exported const name.
- `/packages/spectrum-ts/src/providers/index.ts` (aggregate re-export), `/packages/spectrum-ts/src/providers/<name>/index.ts` (per-provider `export *` shim), `/packages/spectrum-ts/tsdown.config.ts` (entry map), `/packages/spectrum-ts/package.json` (`dependencies` + `exports`)
- Release tooling auto-discovers: `/scripts/release/packages.ts#publishablePackages()` picks up any non-private `packages/*`.

No CLI or onboarding flow lives in this repo (`create-spectrum-app` is external and consumes the manifest).

---

## 5. Commit 36b35b5 — portable `@spectrum-ts/core/webhook`

Files: added `/packages/core/src/webhook/portable.ts`; modified `/packages/core/src/webhook/verify.ts`, `packages/core/package.json` (new `./webhook` export condition), `tsdown.config.ts` (`webhook: "src/webhook/portable.ts"` entry), `biome.jsonc`, `spectrum.ts`, tests.

`portable.ts` re-exports exactly:
- types `SlimContent`, `SlimEnvelope`, `SlimMessage`, `SlimMessageRef`, `SlimSender`, `SlimSpace` and their zod schemas `slimContentSchema`, `slimEnvelopeSchema`, `slimMessageRefSchema`, `slimMessageSchema`, `slimSenderSchema`, `slimSpaceSchema` (from `/packages/core/src/webhook/types.ts` — all `z.looseObject` so additive wire changes don't break older SDKs)
- `verifySpectrumSignature`, `VerifyInput`, `VerifyResult` (from `/packages/core/src/webhook/verify.ts`)

Intent (per the file header): a **runtime-agnostic** surface with zero Node builtins in its import graph — verification runs on Web Crypto via `uncrypto`'s `subtle` — so HTTP adapters on V8-isolate runtimes (Convex, Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy) can verify + parse a native Spectrum webhook where the Node-flavored `Spectrum()` runtime can't run. Signature scheme: `X-Spectrum-Signature: v0=<hex>` = `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "v0:" + timestamp + ":" + rawBody)`, with `X-Spectrum-Timestamp` and a 300s replay window. Deliberately excluded: `/packages/core/src/webhook/deserialize.ts` (materializes full `Content`, pulls `node:fs`/`node:crypto`).

Note: `/docs/webhooks.mdx.vel` does **not** yet document this entry.

---

## 6. Docs

- `/docs/nav.json` — navigation; a new provider needs a `"Providers"` group entry plus a `root` page
- `/docs/providers.mdx.vel` — provider index/card grid + "Combining providers" examples
- `/docs/providers/telegram/setup.mdx.vel` and `/docs/providers/telegram/conversations-and-features.mdx.vel` — best model for a webhook-based external service

- `/docs/integrations/chat-sdk.mdx.vel`, `/docs/integrations/eve.mdx.vel` — the "Integrations" group (non-provider integrations)

Docs use a Velocity-ish template layer (`{% set pd = symbol("ts:spectrum-ts#PlatformDef") %}`) that generates field tables directly from TS symbols, so `PlatformDef` doc comments feed the published tables.

## 7. Guides / generators / templates

- **`/docs/custom-platforms.mdx.vel`** (297 lines) — *the* authoritative "Building a Custom Platform" guide: platform-ID rules, a complete `definePlatform` skeleton, and a full field reference table for `PlatformDef` and its nested slots. This is your primary spec.

If sim.ai pushes events over HTTP, model it on **Telegram** (fusor mode: `createClient` returns `fusor("sim_ai", verify(config))`, `messages` is a typed `FusorMessages` reference so the fusor overload is selected — see the overload-resolution comment at define.ts:325-337). 1	---
2	title: "Chat SDK"
3	description: "Add iMessage to a Chat SDK bot with the iMessage adapter"
4	---
5	
6	The iMessage adapter (`chat-adapter-imessage`) connects [Chat SDK](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs) bots to iMessage. It's built on [`spectrum-ts`](/spectrum-ts/introduction), so the same bot code reaches iMessage through any of three modes:
7	
8	<Note>
9	  Building an agent with [eve](https://vercel.com/eve)? Follow the [eve
10	  integration guide](/integrations/eve) to provision Photon and add
11	  iMessage as an eve channel.
12	</Note>
13	
14	- **Cloud** (recommended) — connects to [Spectrum Cloud](https://app.photon.codes) with a project ID and secret. Runs anywhere, including serverless.
15	- **Self-hosted** — connects to your own `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` gRPC endpoint.
16	- **Local** — reads the on-device Messages database and sends through Apple's native APIs. macOS only.
17	
18	The mode is auto-detected from the options you pass (and their environment-variable fallbacks). See [Configuration](#configuration).
19	
20	## Installation
21	
22	```bash
23	pnpm add chat chat-adapter-imessage
24	```
25	
26	`chat` is the Chat SDK; `chat-adapter-imessage` is the iMessage adapter for it.
27	
28	## Add the adapter
29	
30	Register the adapter under `adapters.imessage` when you construct your bot, then handle messages with the usual Chat SDK callbacks.
31	
32	<Tabs>
33	  <Tab title="Cloud">
34	    Connects to Spectrum Cloud over gRPC. Get your project ID and secret from the [dashboard](https://app.photon.codes).
35	
36	    ```ts
37	    import { Chat } from "chat";
38	    import { createiMessageAdapter } from "chat-adapter-imessage";
39	
40	    const bot = new Chat({
41	      userName: "mybot",
42	      adapters: {
43	        imessage: createiMessageAdapter({
44	          local: false,
45	          projectId: process.env.IMESSAGE_PROJECT_ID,
46	          projectSecret: process.env.IMESSAGE_PROJECT_SECRET,
47	        }),
48	      },
49	    });
50	
51	    bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message) => {
52	      await thread.post("Hello from iMessage!");
53	    });
54	    ```
55	  </Tab>
56	  <Tab title="Self-hosted">
57	    Points the adapter at your own `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` gRPC server.
58	
59	    ```ts
60	    const bot = new Chat({
61	      userName: "mybot",
62	      adapters: {
63	        imessage: createiMessageAdapter({
64	          local: false,
65	          serverUrl: process.env.IMESSAGE_SERVER_URL,
66	          apiKey: process.env.IMESSAGE_API_KEY,
67	        }),
68	      },
69	    });
70	    ```
71	
72	    For multi-number setups, pass explicit `clients` instead of `serverUrl`/`apiKey`:
73	
74	    ```ts
75	    createiMessageAdapter({
76	      local: false,
77	      clients: [
78	        { address: "imessage.example.com:443", token: "…", phone: "+1234567890" },
79	      ],
80	    });
81	    ```
82	
83	    <Warning>
84	      `serverUrl` is a gRPC `host:port` (e.g. `imessage.example.com:443`), **not** an `https://` URL. A bare host gets `:443` appended; any URL scheme is stripped.
85	    </Warning>
86	  </Tab>
87	  <Tab title="Local">
88	    Runs directly on a Mac — reads the local Messages database and sends on-device, with no external server. Requires macOS with **Full Disk Access** granted to your terminal or application, and iMessage signed in.
89	
90	    ```ts
91	    const bot = new Chat({
92	      userName: "mybot",
93	      adapters: {
94	        imessage: createiMessageAdapter({ local: true }),
95	      },
96	    });
97	    ```
98	  </Tab>
99	</Tabs>
100	
101	## Configuration
102	
103	`createiMessageAdapter(options)` accepts the options below. Each has an environment-variable fallback, so you can configure the adapter entirely through the environment and pass no arguments.
104	
105	| Option | Required | Description |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `local` | No | `true` for local, `false` for cloud/self-host. Defaults to local unless `local: false`, `IMESSAGE_LOCAL=false`, or remote credentials are provided. |
108	| `projectId` | Cloud | Spectrum Cloud project ID. Falls back to `IMESSAGE_PROJECT_ID`. |
109	| `projectSecret` | Cloud | Spectrum Cloud project secret. Falls back to `IMESSAGE_PROJECT_SECRET`. |
110	| `serverUrl` | Self-host | gRPC `host:port` of your iMessage server. Falls back to `IMESSAGE_SERVER_URL`. |
111	| `apiKey` | Self-host | Auth token for the self-hosted server. Falls back to `IMESSAGE_API_KEY`. |
112	| `clients` | No | Explicit `{ address, token, phone }[]` for multi-number self-host setups. |
113	| `phone` | No | Routing/identity phone for legacy self-host (defaults to `"shared"`). Falls back to `IMESSAGE_PHONE`. |
114	| `webhookSecret` | No | Per-webhook signing secret for verifying Spectrum Cloud deliveries. Required to receive [webhooks](#webhooks). Falls back to `IMESSAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |
115	| `logger` | No | Logger instance (defaults to `ConsoleLogger("info")`). |
116	
117	### Environment variables
118	
119	```bash
120	# .env.local
121	IMESSAGE_LOCAL=false                  # "false" for cloud/self-host (default: true)
122	
123	# Cloud (recommended)
124	IMESSAGE_PROJECT_ID=...
125	IMESSAGE_PROJECT_SECRET=...
126	
127	# Self-hosted (alternative)
128	IMESSAGE_SERVER_URL=imessage.example.com:443   # gRPC host:port (NOT an https URL)
129	IMESSAGE_API_KEY=...
130	IMESSAGE_PHONE=+1234567890                      # optional, for multi-number routing
131	
132	# Webhooks (remote/cloud only)
133	IMESSAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...               # per-webhook signing secret
134	```
135	
136	## Receiving messages
137	
138	There are two ways to receive inbound messages:
139	
140	- **Webhooks** (recommended for serverless) — Spectrum Cloud delivers each message to an HTTPS endpoint as signed JSON. No long-lived connection or cron job. Cloud mode only.
141	- **Gateway listener** — `startGatewayListener()` consumes spectrum-ts's message stream in real time. Works in all modes; in serverless it needs a cron job to stay connected.
142	
143	### Webhooks
144	
145	In cloud mode, [Spectrum Cloud](https://app.photon.codes) delivers inbound messages to your HTTPS endpoint as signed JSON — see the [webhook docs](/webhooks/overview). This is the simplest path for serverless: no cron, no persistent connection.
146	
147	<Steps>
148	  <Step title="Register the endpoint">
149	    In the [Spectrum Cloud dashboard](https://app.photon.codes), register your endpoint URL (public HTTPS only) and copy the per-webhook **signing secret** — it is shown only once.
150	  </Step>
151	  <Step title="Configure the secret">
152	    Set `IMESSAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to that signing secret. The adapter verifies the `X-Spectrum-Signature` HMAC on every delivery and rejects unsigned, mismatched, or stale (>5 min) requests.
153	
154	    ```bash
155	    IMESSAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...
156	    ```
157	  </Step>
158	  <Step title="Create the webhook route">
159	    ```ts
160	    // app/api/imessage/webhook/route.ts
161	    import { after } from "next/server";
162	    import { bot } from "@/lib/bot";
163	
164	    export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
165	      return bot.webhooks.imessage(request, {
166	        waitUntil: (task) => after(() => task),
167	      });
168	    }
169	    ```
170	
171	    `bot.webhooks.imessage` verifies the signature, parses the `messages` event, and routes the message into your bot. Processing runs in the background via `waitUntil`, so the endpoint acknowledges immediately.
172	  </Step>
173	</Steps>
174	
175	Spectrum Cloud retries failed deliveries with backoff and delivers at-least-once — dedupe on `X-Spectrum-Webhook-Id` + `message.id` if you need exactly-once side effects.
176	
177	A webhook delivery carries no live connection, but your bot can still respond to a **DM**: the adapter rebuilds the thread from its address and sends, reacts, edits, and shows typing over spectrum-ts — no gateway needed.
178	
179	```ts
180	bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message) => {
181	  await thread.post("Got it!"); // works directly from a webhook delivery (DM)
182	});
183	```
184	
185	Replying into a **group** still requires that group to have been received over the gateway listener in the same session — see [Limitations](#limitations).
186	
187	### Gateway listener for serverless
188	
189	The gateway listener keeps a live spectrum-ts stream open. In serverless, run it on a cron so it reconnects before each window expires.
190	
191	<Steps>
192	  <Step title="Create the gateway route">
193	    ```ts
194	    // app/api/imessage/gateway/route.ts
195	    import { after } from "next/server";
196	    import { bot } from "@/lib/bot";
197	
198	    export const maxDuration = 800;
199	
200	    export async function GET(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
201	      const cronSecret = process.env.CRON_SECRET;
202	      if (!cronSecret) {
203	        return new Response("CRON_SECRET not configured", { status: 500 });
204	      }
205	
206	      const authHeader = request.headers.get("authorization");
207	      if (authHeader !== `Bearer ${cronSecret}`) {
208	        return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
209	      }
210	
211	      const durationMs = 600 * 1000;
212	
213	      return bot.adapters.imessage.startGatewayListener(
214	        { waitUntil: (task) => after(() => task) },
215	        durationMs
216	      );
217	    }
218	    ```
219	  </Step>
220	  <Step title="Configure Vercel Cron">
221	    ```json
222	    // vercel.json
223	    {
224	      "crons": [
225	        {
226	          "path": "/api/imessage/gateway",
227	          "schedule": "*/9 * * * *"
228	        }
229	      ]
230	    }
231	    ```
232	
233	    This runs every 9 minutes, overlapping the 10-minute listener duration so the stream is never down. Vercel adds `CRON_SECRET` automatically when you configure cron jobs.
234	  </Step>
235	</Steps>
236	
237	## Feature support
238	
239	"Remote" below means cloud or self-hosted mode — anything other than `local: true`.
240	
241	<Accordion title="Feature support" description="Which Chat SDK capabilities the iMessage adapter implements, by mode.">
242	  | Feature | Supported |
243	  |---|---|
244	  | Mentions | DMs only |
245	  | DMs | Yes |
246	  | File uploads | Yes (send) |
247	  | Reactions (add) | Remote only |
248	  | Reactions (remove) | No |
249	  | Message editing | Remote only |
250	  | Typing indicator | Remote only |
251	  | Modals | Limited (remote only) |
252	  | Message history | No |
253	  | Thread/chat info | No |
254	  | Cards | No |
255	  | Streaming | No |
256	  | Ephemeral messages | No |
257	  | Webhooks | Yes (remote — Spectrum Cloud delivery) |
258	</Accordion>
259	
260	## Modals
261	
262	Remote mode supports limited modals by mapping Chat SDK's `openModal()` to iMessage native polls. Only `Select` children are supported — the first `Select` in the modal becomes a poll:
263	
264	- `Modal.title` becomes the poll question.
265	- `Select.options` become the poll choices (2–10 supported).
266	- Votes trigger `onModalSubmit` with the selected option's `value`.
267	
268	```ts
269	import { Chat, Modal, Select, SelectOption } from "chat";
270	import { createiMessageAdapter } from "chat-adapter-imessage";
271	
272	const bot = new Chat({
273	  userName: "mybot",
274	  adapters: {
275	    imessage: createiMessageAdapter({ local: false }),
276	  },
277	});
278	
279	bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message) => {
280	  await message.openModal(
281	    Modal({
282	      callbackId: "fav-color",
283	      title: "What is your favorite color?",
284	      children: [
285	        Select({
286	          id: "color",
287	          label: "Pick a color",
288	          options: [
289	            SelectOption({ label: "Red", value: "red" }),
290	            SelectOption({ label: "Blue", value: "blue" }),
291	            SelectOption({ label: "Green", value: "green" }),
292	          ],
293	        }),
294	      ],
295	    })
296	  );
297	});
298	
299	bot.onModalSubmit("fav-color", async (event) => {
300	  const color = event.values.color; // "red", "blue", or "green"
301	});
302	```
303	
304	Polls in the same chat must have distinct titles — votes are matched back to the modal by title. Local mode throws `NotImplementedError`.
305	
306	<Note>
307	  Not supported: `Select.placeholder`/`label`, `TextInput`, `RadioSelect`, `Modal.submitLabel`/`closeLabel`, more than one `Select`, and poll vote deselection.
308	</Note>
309	
310	## Tapback reactions
311	
312	iMessage uses tapbacks instead of emoji reactions. The adapter maps standard emoji names to iMessage tapbacks.
313	
314	<Accordion title="Tapback mapping" description="Emoji names accepted by addReaction and the iMessage tapback each maps to.">
315	  | Emoji name | Tapback |
316	  |---|---|
317	  | `love` / `heart` | Love |
318	  | `like` / `thumbs_up` | Like |
319	  | `dislike` / `thumbs_down` | Dislike |
320	  | `laugh` | Laugh |
321	  | `emphasize` / `exclamation` | Emphasize |
322	  | `question` | Question |
323	</Accordion>
324	
325	## Limitations
326	
327	- **DMs send cold; groups are session-bound.** For a **DM**, the adapter rebuilds the thread from its address over gRPC, so it can send, react, edit, and show typing even into a thread it hasn't seen this session — including a webhook delivery. A **group** has no by-id resolver, so addressing one requires it to have been received over the gateway/stream in the current session; cold sends to an unseen group throw `NotImplementedError`. Local mode cannot create spaces at all — it only replies to received messages.
328	- **No message history.** `fetchMessages` is not supported — spectrum-ts exposes no paginated history API.
329	- **No thread/chat info.** `fetchThread` is not supported.
330	- **No reaction removal.** `removeReaction` is not supported.
331	- **Local mode** supports sending and receiving, but not reactions, typing, editing, modals, history, or thread info.
332	- **Formatting.** iMessage is plain-text only; Markdown formatting is stripped when sending, preserving the text content.
333	- **Platform.** Local mode requires macOS. Cloud and self-host run anywhere.
334	- **Cards.** iMessage has no structured card layouts.
335	
336	## Troubleshooting
337	
338	<AccordionGroup>
339	  <Accordion title="serverUrl is required when local is false">
340	    Provide cloud credentials (`IMESSAGE_PROJECT_ID` + `IMESSAGE_PROJECT_SECRET`), or a self-host `IMESSAGE_SERVER_URL` + `IMESSAGE_API_KEY`.
341	  </Accordion>
342	  <Accordion title="Self-host connection issues">
343	    Confirm `IMESSAGE_SERVER_URL` is a gRPC `host:port` (e.g. `imessage.example.com:443`), not an `https://` URL. Verify the token matches your server's credentials.
344	  </Accordion>
345	  <Accordion title="Local mode not receiving messages">
346	    Verify **Full Disk Access** is granted to your terminal or application, and that iMessage is signed in and working on the Mac.
347	  </Accordion>
348	  <Accordion title="NotImplementedError from fetchMessages / fetchThread / removeReaction">
349	    These are not supported by spectrum-ts. See [Limitations](#limitations).
350	  </Accordion>
351	</AccordionGroup>
352

## Open questions (pending codebase exploration)

- What exactly a "channel" is in Photon (messaging surface vs. reply backend) and which side Sim should plug into.

input.new_string:
## Research: Photon architecture findings

- No "channel" type in spectrum-ts. Two integration shapes exist:
  - **Providers** (`definePlatform("id", ...)` packages, e.g. `@spectrum-ts/imessage`) = messaging surfaces (inbound `messages` iterable + outbound `send`). Sim is NOT a messaging surface — a Sim provider doesn't fit (`PlatformDef` models humans-in, bot-out; Sim is the bot).
  - **Integrations** (docs group `integrations/`: `chat-sdk.mdx.vel`, `eve.mdx.vel`) = external agent products connected to iMessage *through* Photon. eve literally calls this a "channel" (`eve add channel/photon-imessage`). **This is the matching shape for sim.ai**: Sim workflow = agent brain; Photon imessage provider = surface; a bridge forwards inbound iMessages to Sim and replies with workflow output.
- App-level consumption pattern (from `examples/basic/index.ts`):
  `const app = await Spectrum({ providers: [imessage.config({...})] })`, then `for await (const [space, message] of app.messages)` → `message.reply(text(...))` / `space.send(...)`.
- iMessage cannot stream tokens (eve doc: "Replies are sent as complete messages") → buffer Sim SSE to completion; use typing indicator while waiting.
- Conversation continuity: map Photon `space.id` → Sim `conversationId` (chat deployment API keeps history server-side).
- Docs nav: add page under `Integrations` group in `docs/nav.json`.
- Examples convention: `examples/basic` = tiny package.json (`private`, dep `spectrum-ts: workspace:*`, bun start script) + single `index.ts`.
- Relevant repo conventions: Bun + Turbo workspaces; provider packages have turbo tag `provider` (bridge package would NOT be a provider — no `spectrum` manifest field, not in metapackage `providers/`); authoring helpers from `@spectrum-ts/core/authoring` (`tracedFetch`, `createLogger`, `envAwareConfig`/`fromEnv`); env conventions `SPECTRUM_*`.

## Deliverable shape options (to confirm with user)

1. Docs-only guide `docs/integrations/sim.mdx.vel` with inline bridge code.
2. Example app `examples/sim-imessage` + docs guide.
3. Reusable package `packages/sim` (`@spectrum-ts/sim`) exporting a provider-agnostic `connectSim(app, opts)` bridge + docs guide (+ optional example). Closest to eve's "channel" artifact.

## Sim API mode options (to confirm with user)

- Chat deployment endpoint (`POST /api/chat/{slug}`, conversationId → server-side history) — recommended default for a messaging bridge.
- Workflow execute API (`POST /api/v2/workflows/{id}/execute`, x-api-key, stateless — workflow manages its own memory).
- Both via discriminated config union (pattern exists: whatsapp-business `z.union`).

## Pending

## Terminology first

This repo has **no `Channel` class** — the abstraction is called a **provider / platform**, created via `definePlatform(...)`. Two important corrections up front:

- **"Eve" is not an implementation in this repo.** `docs/integrations/eve.mdx.vel` (commit `041e7a7`) documents an *external* eve agent channel (`eve add channel/photon-imessage`) that wraps `photon-hq/vercel-chat-adapter-imessage`, which itself sits on `spectrum-ts`. No eve code lives here.

# 2. Interfaces implemented

There is one interface, `PlatformDef`, defined in **`/Users/qwerzl/Documents/Projects/spectrum-ts/packages/core/src/platform/types.ts:275`**. It is consumed by `definePlatform` in **`packages/core/src/platform/define.ts:338`**, which has **two overloads**:

- **regular mode** — `lifecycle.createClient` returns an SDK client; `messages` is a long-lived `EventProducer` async-iterable.
- **fusor mode** — `createClient` returns `fusor(name, verify)` (a branded `FusorClient`); `messages` becomes a per-webhook handler typed `FusorMessages<TPayload, TConfig>` (`packages/core/src/fusor/types.ts:48`).

The overload is selected by whether `messages` is a *typed reference* (non-context-sensitive → fusor) or an inline arrow (deferred → regular). See the long comment at `define.ts:314-337`.

Required members (`PlatformDef`): `name`, `config`, `lifecycle.createClient`, `user.resolve`, `space.create`, `messages`, `send`.
Optional: `lifecycle.destroyClient`, `space.get`, `space.schema`, `space.params`, `space.actions`, `message.schema`, `message.actions`, `actions` (platform-wise + platform-specific), `events`, `static`.

Platform-wise action names are fixed by `PlatformWiseActions` (`platform/types.ts:93`) and the runtime set `PLATFORM_WISE_ACTION_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/platform/build.ts:105`: **`getMessage`, `getMembers`, `getAvatar`, `getDisplayName`**. Omitted ones auto-wire to a thrower (`UnsupportedError.action`).

# 3. Config

## Schema + env fallback (automatic)

`definePlatform` wraps every config schema with `envAwareConfig(platformId, def.config)` (`define.ts:526`). `packages/core/src/utils/env.ts:143` rewrites **every string-leaf field** to fall back to `SPECTRUM_<PLATFORM>_<UPPER_SNAKE_KEY>`. Precedence: explicit value > env var > schema default/required. Empty-string env is treated as unset.

**Telegram** — `packages/telegram/src/config.ts:35`:
```ts
export const configSchema = z.object({
  botToken: z.string().regex(BOT_TOKEN_PATTERN, "botToken must be in the form '<id>:<token>'"),
  webhookSecret: z.string().regex(SECRET_TOKEN_PATTERN).optional(),
  baseUrl: z.url().default(DEFAULT_BASE_URL),
```

```ts
  clients: clientEntry.or(z.array(clientEntry)).optional(),   // { address, token, phone }
```

# 4. Inbound flow

## Telegram (webhook, via Fusor)

1. **Registration** — `createClient` calls `ensureWebhook` (`src/webhook.ts:39`), which is idempotent: `getWebhookInfo` → only `setWebhook` when the URL differs. Target URL is `https://{slug}.spctrm.dev/telegram`.
2. **Delivery** — Telegram POSTs to the Fusor edge, which forwards a protobuf `RawInboundEvent` (whose `rawRequest` is the original HTTP/1.1 wire bytes) over either the Fusor WebSocket (`packages/core/src/fusor/websocket.ts`, started lazily on first `spectrum.messages` read) or a direct `spectrum.webhook(request, handler)` call.
3. **Route + verify** — `FusorCore.processEvent` (`packages/core/src/fusor/core.ts:327`) looks handlers up by `event.platform`, parses the inner request via `parseHttpRequest`, then `runHandlerOnce` calls `handler.verify(parsedRequest)`:
   ```ts
   // packages/telegram/src/verify.ts:63
   export const verify = (config: TelegramConfig): FusorVerify<TelegramPayload> =>
     (req: FusorVerifyRequest): TelegramPayload => {
       if (config.webhookSecret) verifySecret(req.headers, config.webhookSecret);
       return parseUpdate(new TextDecoder().decode(req.rawBody));
     };
   ```
   A throw → 400, no retry. Secret check is `timingSafeEqual` on `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`.
4. **Map** — `handleMessages` (`src/inbound/messages.ts:123`) returns one `ProviderMessageRecord | undefined`. Self-echo is dropped via `botIdFromToken`; captioned media becomes `asGroup([caption, media])`; reactions get a synthetic id `reaction:{chat}:{msg}:{date}:{actor}:{emoji}`.
5. **Dispatch** — `routeHandlerResult` (`fusor/core.ts:106`) sends the record to `handler.pushMessage` → the per-platform `AsyncQueue` created at `spectrum.ts:602` → `createProviderMessagesStream` (`spectrum.ts:451`) → `resolveRecordToMessages` (`spectrum.ts:392`) which calls `buildSpace` + `wrapProviderMessage(record, …, "inbound")`, optionally flattening `group` content into N messages → `broadcast(...)` → `for await (const [space, message] of app.messages)`.

## iMessage (long-lived gRPC streams)

`messages: ({ client, projectConfig }) => remoteMessages(client, projectConfig, getProfileSyncGate(client))` — `packages/imessage/src/remote/stream.ts:499`.

Per configured line it merges **three** resumable streams (`messageStream`, `pollStream`, `groupStream`, the last only in dedicated mode), each built with `resumableOrderedStream` from `@spectrum-ts/core/authoring`: `subscribeLive` + `fetchMissed(cursor)` catch-up + per-event cursor. The line set is dynamic, so `createStreamGroup` + `addLineObserver` add/remove lines when cloud token renewal reconciles them (`src/auth.ts:163`). Self-echo is suppressed by `isFromMe`/actor checks. Non-retryable mapping throws become empty skip items so the cursor advances (`skipUnmappable`, `stream.ts:94`). Downstream the records enter the exact same `resolveRecordToMessages` pipeline as Telegram.

---

# 5. Outbound flow

## Telegram

`send` (`src/outbound/send.ts:158`) builds a fresh client per call (`telegramClient(config)` — cheap, no network), then:
```ts
const sendContent = async (client, space, content) => {
  const spec = await buildSend(content);
  const sent = await executeSpec(client, { ...spec, params: { chat_id: space.id, ...spec.params } });
  return { id: String(sent.message_id), content, space: { id: space.id }, timestamp: new Date(sent.date * 1000) };
};
```
- `buildSend` (`src/outbound/message.ts:88`) maps content → `{ method, params, file? }`: `sendMessage` / `sendPhoto` / `sendVideo` / `sendDocument` / `sendVoice`; `markdown` → `markdownToTelegramHtml` + `parse_mode: "HTML"`; `reply` recurses and adds `reply_parameters`; `custom` is an escape hatch to any Bot API method.
- **No text chunking anywhere in this repo** — neither provider splits long text.
- **Media out**: `executeSpec` (`src/client.ts:77`) posts JSON normally; with `spec.file` it wraps bytes in a `File`, uses a hand-rolled `toFormData` serializer and sets `Content-Type: null` so fetch computes the multipart boundary.
- **Media in**: `downloadFile` (`src/client.ts:108`) — `getFile` for the path, then one authenticated `fetch` through `tracedFetch("telegram", { redactUrl: redactBotToken })`. Attachments are lazy (`read: lazyRead(config, file.file_id)` in `src/inbound/media.ts`).
- `group` → N separate sends, last record returned. `reaction` → `setMessageReaction` with an allowlist pre-check, synthetic id returned. `typing` → `sendChatAction` (no "stop"). `read` → silent no-op. `streamText` → `sendMessageDraft` at 500 ms throttle, then a real `sendMessage` (`src/outbound/stream-text.ts`). Unsupported (`poll`, `effect`, `rename`, `avatar`, membership) throw `UnsupportedError.content`.

## iMessage

`send` (`src/index.ts:636`) routes by `content.type` to `clientForPhone(client, space.phone)` and the RPC wrappers in `src/remote/api.ts`. Every message-producing send passes through `cacheRemoteOutbound` (`index.ts:124`) which writes into the per-client LRU message cache — this is what lets inbound reactions/read-receipts resolve their targets. Guards: group-only for `rename`/`avatar`/`addMember`/`removeMember`/`leaveSpace`/`getMembers`/`getAvatar`/`getDisplayName` (`remoteGroupClient`, `index.ts:380`); polls reject `reply`/`react`/`unsend`. `streamText` sends the first chunk then edits it in place (`src/remote/stream-text.ts`). Attachments stream over gRPC in `primaryChunk` frames (`src/remote/attachments.ts`).

# 6. Registration — the exact places a new channel must be added

For an in-repo provider named `my_platform` in `packages/my-platform/`:

1. **`packages/my-platform/package.json`** — name `@spectrum-ts/my-platform`; `"type": "module"`; `exports` with the `bun`/`types`/`default` triple plus the `publishConfig.exports` override; `peerDependencies: { "@spectrum-ts/core": "^12.0.0", "typescript": "^5 || ^6.0.0" }`; devDeps `@spectrum-ts/core: workspace:*`, `@spectrum-ts/test-support: workspace:*`, `tsdown`, `vitest`; scripts `build` (`tsdown && node ../../scripts/smoke-import.mjs dist/index.js`), `dev`, `test:bun`, `test:node`, `typecheck`; **and the manifest block**:
   ```json
   "spectrum": { "key": "my_platform", "import": "myPlatform", "label": "my_platform" }
   ```
2. **`packages/my-platform/src/index.ts`** — must literally match `/^export\s+const\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*definePlatform\(\s*(?:"([^"]+)"|(\w+))/m`, i.e. `export const myPlatform = definePlatform(MY_PLATFORM, {...})`. `generate-manifest.ts:70` validates that `import` === the exported const name and `label` === the platform id (resolving a shared const from any `src/*.ts` if not inline). Mismatch = build failure.
3. **`packages/my-platform/turbo.json`** — `{ "extends": ["//"], "tags": ["provider"] }`. The `provider` tag makes `turbo boundaries` forbid importing other providers.
4. **`tsconfig.json`** (`extends ../../tsconfig.json`, `include: ["src","test"]`, `paths: {"@/*": ["./src/*"]}`), **`tsdown.config.ts`**, **`vitest.config.ts`** (`spectrumTestConfig(import.meta.dirname)`), `LICENSE`, `README.md`.
5. **`packages/core/src/utils/provider-packages.ts:14`** — add `my_platform: "@spectrum-ts/my-platform"` to `OFFICIAL_PROVIDER_PACKAGES` so "no handler for platform" warnings emit an install hint.
6. **If batteries-included**: add to `packages/spectrum-ts/package.json` dependencies (pinned exact version), create the shim `packages/spectrum-ts/src/providers/my-platform/index.ts` (`export * from "@spectrum-ts/my-platform";` — a pure star export, deliberately), add a named re-export to `packages/spectrum-ts/src/providers/index.ts`, and add the pair to the `cases` array in `packages/spectrum-ts/test/providers-shims.test.ts`. (iMessage-local skips all of step 6 and has no `spectrum` field — see `packages/spectrum-ts/test/imessage-package-boundary.test.ts`.)
7. **Docs**: `docs/providers/my-platform.mdx.vel` + subpages, a card in `docs/providers.mdx.vel`, and a group entry in **`docs/nav.json`** under `"Providers"`.
8. **Nothing else.** Root `package.json` uses `workspaces: ["packages/*"]`, and `scripts/release/packages.ts` auto-discovers every non-private package under `packages/`.

Runtime registration is fully dynamic — `Spectrum()` iterates `providers` and stores `platformStates.set(def.name, …)` (`spectrum.ts:569`); fusor providers additionally self-register at `spectrum.ts:655` via `fusorCore.register(client.platform, handler)`. The `fusor(...)` key, the `definePlatform` name, and Fusor's URL path segment **must be the same string** — see the comment at `packages/telegram/src/config.ts:3-17`.

# Minimal template for a new HTTP/webhook channel

```ts
// packages/my-platform/src/config.ts
export const MY_PLATFORM = "my_platform";              // must match fusor key + Fusor path segment
export const configSchema = z.object({ apiKey: z.string(), webhookSecret: z.string().optional() });

// packages/my-platform/src/index.ts
export const myPlatform = definePlatform(MY_PLATFORM, {
```

1	---
2	title: Architecture
3	description: Patterns for building human-feeling agents on Spectrum
4	---
5	
6	<Note>
7	This is the architecture we use at Photon to ship agents that **live natively inside IM apps**.
8	
9	The patterns below are pulled directly from production, based on the problems we encountered and the solutions we built to solve them. They're not theoretical best practices - they're the ones that **worked in the real world, with real users, and real bugs**. If you're building a similar agent, these patterns will save you **months** of trial and error.
10	</Note>
11	
12	A naive Spectrum agent - read incoming, call the LLM, send the reply - falls apart in ways you don't see until you ship it. The user types "hey" → "wait" → "actually nvm" inside three seconds and gets three independent responses. The agent replies in 200ms when a real person would take five minutes. A worker crashes mid-send and the user receives the same message twice on retry.
13	
14	This section captures the patterns that solve those problems, drawn from production agents built on Spectrum.
15	
16	## The pipeline
17	
18	Every incoming message flows through five stages backed by a job queue. Each stage is a separately enqueued job, which is what makes any of them cancellable when a follow-up message lands.
19	
20	```mermaid
21	flowchart LR
22	  In([Incoming message]) --> BQ[(Batch queue)]
23	  BQ -->|debounce window| Flush[Batch flush]
24	  Flush --> Read[Mark as read]
25	  Read --> Gen[Generate reply]
26	  Gen --> Send[Send with pacing]
27	  Send --> Done([Done])
28	
29	  Inflight[(In-flight table)] -.tracks.- Flush
30	  Inflight -.tracks.- Read
31	  Inflight -.tracks.- Gen
32	  Inflight -.tracks.- Send
33	```
34	
35	The `In-flight` table is a per-chat record of whichever job ID currently owns each stage. When a new message arrives, the enqueuer reads it, cancels those jobs, and moves any messages that were already drained into a carry-forward table so the next batch sees them.
36	
37	## Why split it up
38	
39	If you do everything in one handler - read, generate, send - you lose the ability to react to a new message that arrives during generation. By the time you notice, you've already sent a reply that ignored what the user just said, or you've raced the LLM against itself.
40	
41	Splitting into stages costs a few hundred ms of extra hop latency and buys you:
42	
43	- **Cancellation points.** Each stage can check a flag and abort cleanly.
44	- **Resume points.** A worker crash mid-stage retries one stage, not the whole conversation turn.
45	- **Idempotency seams.** The send stage carries stable client GUIDs so retries don't double-send.
46	- **Distinct timing.** The read stage can sleep for an hour while the send stage runs in 500ms - they're independent jobs.
47	
48	## What's in this section
49	
50	- [Inbound pipeline](/best-practices/inbound-pipeline) - debouncing message bursts, batching, surviving cancellation, and the carry-forward rule that keeps messages from getting lost.
51	- [Recovery and state](/best-practices/recovery-and-state) - idempotent retries via client GUIDs, per-resource memory scope, and a durable failure audit log.

# Plan: iMessage (Photon) integration for Sim's catalog (sim.ai/integrations)

## Context

Goal: get iMessage — powered by Photon / `spectrum-ts` — listed on https://www.sim.ai/integrations, so Sim workflows can receive and send iMessages. Sim's catalog is generated from its open-source repo, so "submitting" = a PR to `simstudioai/sim` (target branch `staging`) adding a block + tool + webhook trigger. Sim currently has telegram/whatsapp/twilio/sms but **no iMessage** — no naming collision, genuine gap.

Best-practice sources found (per user request):
- Sim's canonical recipes: `.agents/skills/add-integration/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/add-trigger/SKILL.md` in `simstudioai/sim` (authoritative; re-read them from the fork before implementing).
- Sim PR rules: branch `feat/...` off `staging`, Conventional Commits, `bun run type-check && lint:check && test` before PR.
- spectrum-ts side: `docs/webhooks.mdx.vel` (native webhook = HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<ts>:<rawBody>`, headers `X-Spectrum-Signature: v0=<hex>` + `X-Spectrum-Timestamp`, 5-min replay window, at-least-once ⇒ dedupe on `message.id`), portable verifier `@spectrum-ts/core/webhook` (`verifySpectrumSignature`, Slim* zod schemas in `packages/core/src/webhook/types.ts` — commit 36b35b5 built this exact use case), and `docs/best-practices/*` (complete-message replies; iMessage can't stream).

Verified feasibility facts:
- Sim tools whose work isn't a plain HTTP call use **internal Next.js routes** (`request.url: '/api/tools/{service}/...'`) — e.g. `postgresql_query` → `/api/tools/postgresql/query`, creds as `visibility: 'user-only'` params. Heavy SDK deps in `apps/sim/package.json` are precedented (aws-sdk, mongodb, mysql2, ssh2). Photon's send path is gRPC (`nice-grpc`), so send goes through an internal route using the spectrum-ts SDK.
- Inbound: Photon Cloud delivers signed JSON webhooks (SlimEnvelope) — maps cleanly onto Sim's webhook-trigger provider-handler pattern (`createHmacVerifier`).
- Cold sends work for DMs (adapter rebuilds thread from address); cold group sends are unsupported ⇒ v1 is DM-first.

## Deliverable 1 — PR to `simstudioai/sim`

Workspace: `gh repo fork simstudioai/sim --clone` into `~/Documents/Projects/sim`, branch `feat/photon-imessage-integration` off `staging`. First step: read `.agents/skills/add-integration/SKILL.md` + `add-trigger/SKILL.md` in the clone and follow them exactly (they are the source of truth; the layout below is from today's versions).

Naming (proposed): provider id `photon_imessage`, display name **"iMessage (Photon)"**, tools `photon_imessage_send_message`, trigger `photon_imessage_message_received`, auth = API key style (Photon `projectId` + `projectSecret` from app.photon.codes; no OAuth ⇒ skip Sim's OAuth deployment-capability step).

### Files to create in `apps/sim/`
1. **Tool** `tools/photon_imessage/{types.ts, send_message.ts, index.ts}`
   - Params: `projectId` (user-only), `projectSecret` (user-only, `password: true`), `to` (user-or-llm; phone/email for DM), `spaceId` (advanced alternative target, canonicalParamId rules), `text` (user-or-llm).
   - `request.url: '/api/tools/photon_imessage/send'`; `transformResponse` → `{ messageId, spaceId, timestamp }` with `?? null` guards.
2. **Internal route** `app/api/tools/photon_imessage/send/route.ts` + contract `lib/api/contracts/tools/photon_imessage.ts`
   - `checkInternalAuth` first, zod contract parse, then send via spectrum-ts: module-level LRU of `Spectrum({ projectId, projectSecret, providers: [imessage.config()] })` instances keyed by projectId+secret hash (mint/reconcile on `createClient` is too costly per-call); resolve space from `to` (DM `space.create`) or `spaceId`, `space.send(text(...))`.
   - Deps added to `apps/sim/package.json`: `@spectrum-ts/core`, `@spectrum-ts/imessage` (NOT the batteries `spectrum-ts` metapackage).
3. **Trigger** `triggers/photon_imessage/{utils.ts, message_received.ts, index.ts}`
   - `buildTriggerSubBlocks` with `includeDropdown: true`; extra field `webhookSecret` (password); setup instructions: copy Sim webhook URL → register in Photon dashboard (app.photon.codes) → paste signing secret. No `createSubscription` (no public programmatic webhook API).
4. **Webhook provider handler** `lib/webhooks/providers/photon_imessage.ts` + registry entry
   - `verifyAuth`: Photon v0 scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<rawBody>` with timing-safe compare + 5-min replay check. Prefer `verifySpectrumSignature` from `@spectrum-ts/core/webhook` (portable, Web-Crypto, already a dep); must operate on **raw body bytes**.
   - `formatInput`: map SlimEnvelope → outputs (`messageId`, `text`, `senderId`, `spaceId`, `spaceType`, `timestamp`, attachment metadata). Ground truth for field names: `packages/core/src/webhook/types.ts` in spectrum-ts (Sim's hard rule: never guess payload schemas). Keys must exactly match trigger `outputs`.
   - `extractIdempotencyId`: `photon:{message.id}` (at-least-once delivery).
5. **Block** `blocks/blocks/photon_imessage.ts` — `BlockConfig` (type `photon_imessage`, `authMode: AuthMode.ApiKey`, category `tools`, operation dropdown, conditional fields, `tools.access/config`, `triggers: { enabled, available }`, spread trigger subBlocks) + `PhotonImessageBlockMeta` with **≥ 7 templates** (e.g. iMessage support agent, appointment reminders, lead follow-up, iMessage→Slack escalation w/ `alsoIntegrations`, order notifications, feedback collection, on-call alert acknowledgment).
6. **Icon** `components/icons.tsx` → `PhotonImessageIcon`, monochrome `fill='currentColor'` (need Photon brand SVG from user, else a clean message-bubble mark); `bun run check:bare-icons`.
7. **Registries**: `tools/registry.ts`, `blocks/registry-maps.ts` (both BLOCK_REGISTRY + BLOCK_META_REGISTRY), `triggers/registry.ts`, `lib/webhooks/providers/registry.ts` — alphabetical order.
8. **Generated artifacts**: `bun run tool-metadata:generate`, `bun run scripts/generate-docs.ts` (creates `apps/docs/content/docs/en/integrations/photon_imessage.mdx`; edit only the MANUAL-CONTENT block), commit regenerated files.
9. **Tests** (mirror neighbors' tests): HMAC verify (valid/invalid/stale), `formatInput` ↔ outputs alignment, send route contract validation with mocked spectrum-ts.

### PR checks
`bun run type-check`, `lint:check`, `test`, `integration-catalog:check`, `docs:check` — then PR to `staging`, conventional title (e.g. `feat(integrations): add iMessage via Photon`), description linking Photon webhook docs + noting payload schemas come from photon-hq/spectrum-ts source.

## Deliverable 2 — this repo (spectrum-ts): docs page

- `docs/integrations/sim.mdx.vel` mirroring `docs/integrations/eve.mdx.vel`: "Connect a Sim workflow to iMessage through Photon" — provision project, add the block in Sim, webhook registration steps, credential-hygiene warning (project secret ≠ webhook secret), DM-first limitation, link to Sim's generated docs page.
- Add `"integrations/sim"` to the Integrations group in `docs/nav.json`.
- Publish once the Sim PR merges (write now, land together or hold the docs commit).

## Verification

1. In the sim fork: run the five check commands above; `bun run dev` and in the canvas add the block — trigger UI shows webhook URL + instructions, tag editor shows all output fields.
2. Inbound e2e without Photon: script a signed sample delivery (compute `v0=` HMAC over a SlimEnvelope fixture) → POST to the local trigger URL → workflow run fires once; replayed POST is deduped; tampered signature → 401.
3. Outbound e2e with the user's real Photon project creds: workflow with send block → iMessage arrives on a test handset; second run reuses cached Spectrum instance (no re-mint).
4. spectrum-ts repo: `bun x ultracite check` + docs render for the new page.

## Decisions taken (flag in PR/plan review, easy to change)
- Naming `photon_imessage` / "iMessage (Photon)"; v1 scope = send text + message-received trigger (reactions/typing/attachments as follow-ups); DM-first (cold group send unsupported by design upstream); icon asset needed from Photon brand.

181	serialized shape handling, unchanged ordinary external inputs, malformed/incomplete private metadata
182	failing closed, headerless legacy requests, and absence of private metadata in the public tool result.
183	For durable sinks, also cover legacy `NULL` markers, exact-empty new writes, tracked secret writes,
184	stale/missing sidecars, and scope isolation.

186	## Step 3: Create Block
187	
188	### File Location
189	`apps/sim/blocks/blocks/{service}.ts`
190	
191	### Block Structure
192	```typescript
193	import { {Service}Icon } from '@/components/icons'
194	import type { BlockConfig } from '@/blocks/types'
195	import { AuthMode, IntegrationType } from '@/blocks/types'
196	import { getScopesForService } from '@/lib/oauth/utils'
197	
198	export const {Service}Block: BlockConfig = {
199	  type: '{service}',
200	  name: '{Service}',
201	  description: '...',
202	  longDescription: '...',
203	  docsLink: 'https://docs.sim.ai/integrations/{service}',
204	  category: 'tools',
205	  integrationType: IntegrationType.X,   // Primary category (see IntegrationType enum)
206	  tags: ['oauth', 'api'],              // Cross-cutting tags (see IntegrationTag type)
207	  bgColor: '#HEXCOLOR',
208	  icon: {Service}Icon,
209	  authMode: AuthMode.OAuth,  // or AuthMode.ApiKey
210	
211	  subBlocks: [
212	    // Operation dropdown
213	    {
214	      id: 'operation',
215	      title: 'Operation',
216	      type: 'dropdown',
217	      options: [
218	        { label: 'Operation 1', id: 'action1' },
219	        { label: 'Operation 2', id: 'action2' },
220	      ],
221	      value: () => 'action1',
222	    },
223	    // Credential field
224	    {
225	      id: 'credential',
226	      title: '{Service} Account',
227	      type: 'oauth-input',
228	      serviceId: '{service}',
229	      requiredScopes: getScopesForService('{service}'),
230	      required: true,
231	    },
232	    // Conditional fields per operation
233	    // ...
234	  ],
235	
236	  tools: {
237	    access: ['{service}_action1', '{service}_action2'],
238	    config: {
239	      tool: (params) => `{service}_${params.operation}`,
240	    },
241	  },
242	
243	  outputs: { /* ... */ },
244	}
245	```
246	
247	### Key SubBlock Patterns
248	
249	**Condition-based visibility:**
250	```typescript
251	{
252	  id: 'resourceId',
253	  title: 'Resource ID',
254	  type: 'short-input',
255	  condition: { field: 'operation', value: ['read', 'update', 'delete'] },
256	  required: { field: 'operation', value: ['read', 'update', 'delete'] },
257	}
258	```
259	
260	**DependsOn for cascading selectors:**
261	```typescript
262	{
263	  id: 'project',
264	  type: 'project-selector',
265	  dependsOn: ['credential'],
266	},
267	{
268	  id: 'issue',
269	  type: 'file-selector',
270	  dependsOn: ['credential', 'project'],
271	}
272	```
273	
274	**Basic/Advanced mode for dual UX:**
275	```typescript
276	// Basic: Visual selector
277	{
278	  id: 'channelSelector',
279	  type: 'channel-selector',
280	  mode: 'basic',
281	  canonicalParamId: 'channel',
282	  dependsOn: ['credential'],
283	},
284	// Advanced: Manual input
285	{
286	  id: 'channelId',
287	  type: 'short-input',
288	  mode: 'advanced',
289	  canonicalParamId: 'channel',
290	}
291	```
292	
293	Note neither subblock `id` is `channel` — the canonical id is a third name that both members map
294	onto, and it is the only one that survives serialization.
295	
296	**Critical Canonical Param Rules:**
297	- `canonicalParamId` must NOT match any subblock's `id` in the block
298	- `canonicalParamId` must be unique **block-wide**, not per operation. `buildCanonicalIndex` keys
299	  groups by `canonicalParamId` across all subblocks and a group holds exactly one `basicId`, so two
300	  operations that each need their own pair must use two different canonical ids
301	- Only use `canonicalParamId` to link basic/advanced alternatives for the same logical parameter.
302	  A pair carries ONE concept — for files that means upload (basic) + file reference (advanced), as
303	  in Gmail attachments (`blocks/blocks/gmail.ts`). Never overload the advanced side with alternate
304	  identifiers like a URL or a provider asset ID; give those their own subblocks, mark all the
305	  mutually exclusive sources `required: false`, and enforce "exactly one" at execution
306	- `mode` only controls UI visibility, NOT serialization. Without `canonicalParamId`, both basic and advanced field values would be sent
307	- Every subblock `id` must be unique within the block. Duplicate IDs cause conflicts even with different conditions
308	- **Required consistency:** If one subblock in a canonical group has `required: true`, ALL subblocks in that group must have `required: true` (prevents bypassing validation by switching modes)
309	- **Inputs section:** Must list canonical param IDs (e.g., `fileId`), NOT raw subblock IDs (e.g., `fileSelector`, `manualFileId`)
310	- **Params function:** Must use canonical param IDs, NOT raw subblock IDs (raw IDs are deleted after canonical transformation)
311	
312	### BlockMeta (Required)
313	
314	Export a `{Service}BlockMeta` in the same file as the block — **minimum 7 templates**. See `.agents/skills/add-block/SKILL.md` → "BlockMeta (Required)" for valid `modules` and `category` values and the full pattern.
315	
316	```typescript
317	export const {Service}BlockMeta = {
318	  tags: ['tag1', 'tag2'],
319	  templates: [
320	    {
321	      icon: {Service}Icon,
322	      title: '{Service} <use-case>',
323	      prompt: 'Build a workflow that...',  // concrete trigger → transformation → output
324	      modules: ['agent', 'workflows'],
325	      category: 'operations',
326	      tags: ['automation'],
327	      alsoIntegrations: ['slack'],        // when the prompt references another service
328	    },
329	    // ... at least 6 more
330	  ],
331	} as const satisfies BlockMeta
332	```

334	## Step 4: Add Icon
335	
336	### File Location
337	`apps/sim/components/icons.tsx`
338	
339	### Pattern
340	```typescript
341	export function {Service}Icon(props: SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>) {
342	  return (
343	    <svg
344	      {...props}
345	      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
346	      fill="none"
347	      xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
348	    >
349	      {/* SVG paths from user-provided SVG */}
350	    </svg>
351	  )
352	}
353	```
354	
355	### Getting Icons
356	**Do NOT search for icons yourself.** At the end of implementation, ask the user to provide the SVG:
357	
358	```
359	I've completed the integration. Before I can add the icon, please provide the SVG for {Service}.
360	You can usually find this in the service's brand/press kit page, or copy it from their website.
361	
362	Paste the SVG code here and I'll convert it to a React component.
363	```
364	
365	Once the user provides the SVG:
366	1. Extract the SVG paths/content
367	2. Create a React component that spreads props
368	3. Ensure viewBox is preserved from the original SVG
369	
370	### Theme-safety (bare rendering) — REQUIRED
371	
372	The icon renders both inside its colored `bgColor` tile AND "bare" (no tile) on a
373	neutral page — e.g. the home **Suggested actions** list — in both light and dark
374	mode. A monochrome logo whose paths hardcode a single near-white or near-black
375	fill is invisible bare on the matching background (white-on-white in light mode,
376	black-on-black in dark mode).
377	
378	Rules when adding the SVG:
379	
380	- **Monochrome logos** (a single white or black mark): draw the shape with
381	  `fill='currentColor'`, not `fill='#fff'` / `fill='#000000'`. It then inherits
382	  white inside dark tiles, near-black inside light tiles (via
383	  `getTileIconColorClass`), and the theme-aware `var(--text-icon)` bare — legible
384	  everywhere. Do NOT set `iconColor` for these.
385	- **Multi-color brand logos** (their own vivid fills): keep the hardcoded fills.
386	  They read on any background. Only set `iconColor` (a vivid brand hex, never a
387	  near-black/near-white tile color) if the bare icon should adopt a brand tint.
388	- A large white shape with a tiny vivid accent (e.g. a logo where the body is the
389	  white negative space) still vanishes bare — convert the body to `currentColor`.
390	
391	Verify with `bun run check:bare-icons` (also runs in CI). It flags purely
392	monochrome hazards; for partial-accent logos, eyeball the suggested-actions list
393	in both light and dark mode.

530	## Step 7: Configure Deployment Availability
531	
532	Do this for every visible OAuth integration. API-key and unauthenticated integrations do not need
533	an OAuth client capability.
534	
535	The block's `oauth-input.serviceId` is the canonical link between the generated integration catalog,
536	the OAuth service configuration, deployment availability, and the setup CLI.
537	
538	1. Ensure the block has exactly one distinct OAuth `serviceId` and that it matches the canonical
539	   service entry in `apps/sim/lib/oauth/oauth.ts`.
540	2. Confirm `resolveOAuthClientCapabilityId(serviceId)` resolves to the intended provider entry in
541	   `OAUTH_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES` in `packages/deployment-config/src/env-capabilities.ts`. Google and
542	   Microsoft service IDs deliberately share provider-level capabilities.
543	3. For a new OAuth provider, add the required client fields to `OAUTH_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES`, add
544	   every referenced field to the env schema in `apps/sim/lib/core/config/env.ts`, and add the
545	   matching `text` or `secret` entries to `OAUTH_CLIENT_SETUP_FIELDS` in
546	   `packages/sim-setup/src/capability-config.ts`. Do not create integration-specific setup logic or
547	   infer secret fields from naming; the CLI mapping is exhaustively checked against the runtime
548	   fields.
549	4. If the canonical OAuth service has `serviceAccountProviderId`, run
550	   `bun run deployment-config:generate` to refresh
551	   `packages/deployment-config/src/service-account-providers.generated.ts`; never hand-edit the
552	   generated provider-ID map. In `packages/deployment-config/src/service-account-metadata.ts`, use:
553	   - no `deploymentRequirement` when the service-account path works independently of OAuth client fields;
554	   - `'oauth-client'` when it requires the same deployment OAuth client fields;
555	   - `'preview-gated'` when availability is controlled by the service-account preview block.
556	
557	Never add a permissive fallback for missing capability metadata. A visible OAuth integration without
558	a resolvable capability must fail validation.
