701	## File Handling
702	
703	When your integration handles file uploads or downloads, follow these patterns to work with `UserFile` objects consistently.
704	
705	### What is a UserFile?
706	
707	A `UserFile` is the standard file representation in Sim:
708	
709	```typescript
710	interface UserFile {
711	  id: string       // Unique identifier
712	  name: string     // Original filename
713	  url: string      // Presigned URL for download
714	  size: number     // File size in bytes
715	  type: string     // MIME type (e.g., 'application/pdf')
716	  base64?: string  // Optional base64 content (if small file)
717	  key?: string     // Internal storage key
718	  context?: object // Storage context metadata
719	}
720	```
721	
722	### File Input Pattern (Uploads)
723	
724	For tools that accept file uploads, **always route through an internal API endpoint** rather than calling external APIs directly. This ensures proper file content retrieval.
725	
726	#### 1. Block SubBlocks for File Input
727	
728	Use the basic/advanced mode pattern:
729	
730	```typescript
731	// Basic mode: File upload UI
732	{
733	  id: 'uploadFile',
734	  title: 'File',
735	  type: 'file-upload',
736	  canonicalParamId: 'file',  // Maps to 'file' param
737	  placeholder: 'Upload file',
738	  mode: 'basic',
739	  multiple: false,
740	  required: true,
741	  condition: { field: 'operation', value: 'upload' },
742	},
743	// Advanced mode: Reference from previous block
744	{
745	  id: 'fileRef',
746	  title: 'File',
747	  type: 'short-input',
748	  canonicalParamId: 'file',  // Same canonical param
749	  placeholder: 'Reference file (e.g., {{file_block.output}})',
750	  mode: 'advanced',
751	  required: true,
752	  condition: { field: 'operation', value: 'upload' },
753	},
754	```
755	
756	**Critical:** `canonicalParamId` must NOT match any subblock `id`.
757	
758	#### 2. Normalize File Input in Block Config
759	
760	In `tools.config.tool`, use `normalizeFileInput` to handle all input variants:
761	
762	```typescript
763	import { normalizeFileInput } from '@/blocks/utils'
764	
765	tools: {
766	  config: {
767	    tool: (params) => {
768	      // Normalize file from basic (uploadFile), advanced (fileRef), or legacy (fileContent)
769	      const normalizedFile = normalizeFileInput(
770	        params.uploadFile || params.fileRef || params.fileContent,
771	        { single: true }
772	      )
773	      if (normalizedFile) {
774	        params.file = normalizedFile
775	      }
776	      return `{service}_${params.operation}`
777	    },
778	  },
779	}
780	```
781	
782	#### 3. Create Special Internal Tool Execution Route
783	
784	Create `apps/sim/app/api/tools/{service}/{action}/route.ts`. This raw route pattern is only for an integration's provider-execution boundary when it needs special file normalization, large-body handling, or protocol behavior. It is not the pattern for CRUD or other operations on protected Sim resources. For those, use the `migrate-application-operation` skill and an authorized application use case with the ordinary internal/v2 route builders.
785	
786	Internal tool routes are HTTP boundaries and follow the same contract policy as public routes — define the request/response shape in `apps/sim/lib/api/contracts/tools/{service}.ts` (or an existing aggregate) and validate with canonical helpers from `@/lib/api/server`. Never write a route-local Zod schema. Authenticate and perform cheap admission before parsing or downloading files.
787	
788	```typescript
789	// apps/sim/lib/api/contracts/tools/{service}.ts
790	import { z } from 'zod'
791	import { defineRouteContract } from '@/lib/api/contracts'
792	import { FileInputSchema } from '@/lib/uploads/utils/file-schemas'
793	
794	export const {service}UploadBodySchema = z.object({
795	  accessToken: z.string(),
796	  file: FileInputSchema.optional().nullable(),
797	  fileContent: z.string().optional().nullable(),
798	  // ... other params
799	})
800	
801	export const {service}UploadResponseSchema = z.object({
802	  success: z.boolean(),
803	  output: z.object({ id: z.string(), url: z.string() }).optional(),
804	  error: z.string().optional(),
805	})
806	
807	export const {service}UploadContract = defineRouteContract({
808	  method: 'POST',
809	  path: '/api/tools/{service}/upload',
810	  body: {service}UploadBodySchema,
811	  response: { mode: 'json', schema: {service}UploadResponseSchema },
812	})
813	
814	export type {Service}UploadBody = z.input<typeof {service}UploadBodySchema>
815	export type {Service}UploadResponse = z.output<typeof {service}UploadResponseSchema>
816	```
817	
818	```typescript
819	// apps/sim/app/api/tools/{service}/upload/route.ts
820	import { createLogger } from '@sim/logger'
821	import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from 'next/server'
822	import { {service}UploadContract } from '@/lib/api/contracts/tools/{service}'
823	import { parseRequest } from '@/lib/api/server'
824	import { checkInternalAuth } from '@/lib/auth/hybrid'
825	import { generateRequestId } from '@/lib/core/utils/request'
826	import { withRouteHandler } from '@/lib/core/utils/with-route-handler'
827	import { type RawFileInput } from '@/lib/uploads/utils/file-schemas'
828	import { processFilesToUserFiles } from '@/lib/uploads/utils/file-utils'
829	import { downloadFileFromStorage } from '@/lib/uploads/utils/file-utils.server'
830	
831	const logger = createLogger('{Service}UploadAPI')
832	
833	export const POST = withRouteHandler(async (request: NextRequest) => {
834	  const requestId = generateRequestId()
835	
836	  // Auth always runs BEFORE parseRequest — never validate untrusted input before authenticating.
837	  const authResult = await checkInternalAuth(request, { requireWorkflowId: false })
838	  if (!authResult.success) {
839	    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
840	  }
841	
842	  const parsed = await parseRequest({service}UploadContract, request, {})
843	  if (!parsed.success) return parsed.response
844	  const data = parsed.data.body
845	
846	  let fileBuffer: Buffer
847	  let fileName: string
848	
849	  // Prefer UserFile input, fall back to legacy base64
850	  if (data.file) {
851	    const userFiles = processFilesToUserFiles([data.file as RawFileInput], requestId, logger)
852	    if (userFiles.length === 0) {
853	      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: 'Invalid file' }, { status: 400 })
854	    }
855	    const userFile = userFiles[0]
856	    fileBuffer = await downloadFileFromStorage(userFile, requestId, logger)
857	    fileName = userFile.name
858	  } else if (data.fileContent) {
859	    // Legacy: base64 string (backwards compatibility)
860	    fileBuffer = Buffer.from(data.fileContent, 'base64')
861	    fileName = 'file'
862	  } else {
863	    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: 'File required' }, { status: 400 })
864	  }
865	
866	  // Now call external API with fileBuffer
867	  const response = await fetch('https://api.{service}.com/upload', {
868	    method: 'POST',
869	    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.accessToken}` },
870	    body: new Uint8Array(fileBuffer),  // Convert Buffer for fetch
871	  })
872	
873	  // ... handle response
874	})
875	```
876	
877	#### 4. Update Tool to Use Internal Route
878	
879	```typescript
880	export const {service}UploadTool: ToolConfig<Params, Response> = {
881	  id: '{service}_upload',
882	  // ...
883	  params: {
884	    file: { type: 'file', required: false, visibility: 'user-or-llm' },
885	    fileContent: { type: 'string', required: false, visibility: 'hidden' }, // Legacy
886	  },
887	  request: {
888	    url: '/api/tools/{service}/upload',  // Internal route
889	    method: 'POST',
890	    body: (params) => ({
891	      accessToken: params.accessToken,
892	      file: params.file,
893	      fileContent: params.fileContent,
894	    }),
895	  },
896	}
897	```
898	
899	### File Output Pattern (Downloads)
900	
901	For tools that return files, use `FileToolProcessor` to store files and return `UserFile` objects.
902	
903	#### In Tool transformResponse
904	
905	```typescript
906	import { FileToolProcessor } from '@/executor/utils/file-tool-processor'
907	
908	transformResponse: async (response, context) => {
909	  const data = await response.json()
910	
911	  // Process file outputs to UserFile objects
912	  const fileProcessor = new FileToolProcessor(context)
913	  const file = await fileProcessor.processFileData({
914	    data: data.content,      // base64 or buffer
915	    mimeType: data.mimeType,
916	    filename: data.filename,
917	  })
918	
919	  return {
920	    success: true,
921	    output: { file },
922	  }
923	}
924	```
925	
926	#### In API Route (for complex file handling)
927	
928	```typescript
929	// Return file data that FileToolProcessor can handle
930	return NextResponse.json({
931	  success: true,
932	  output: {
933	    file: {
934	      data: base64Content,
935	      mimeType: 'application/pdf',
936	      filename: 'document.pdf',
937	    },
938	  },
939	})
940	```
941	
942	### Key Helpers Reference
943	
944	| Helper | Location | Purpose |
945	|--------|----------|---------|
946	| `normalizeFileInput` | `@/blocks/utils` | Normalize file params in block config |
947	| `processFilesToUserFiles` | `@/lib/uploads/utils/file-utils` | Convert raw inputs to UserFile[] |
948	| `downloadFileFromStorage` | `@/lib/uploads/utils/file-utils.server` | Get file Buffer from UserFile |
949	| `FileToolProcessor` | `@/executor/utils/file-tool-processor` | Process tool output files |
950	| `isUserFile` | `@/lib/core/utils/user-file` | Type guard for UserFile objects |
951	| `FileInputSchema` | `@/lib/uploads/utils/file-schemas` | Zod schema for file validation |
952	
953	### Advanced Mode for Optional Fields
954	
955	Optional fields that are rarely used should be set to `mode: 'advanced'` so they don't clutter the basic UI. Examples: pagination tokens, time range filters, sort order, max results, reply settings.
956	
957	### WandConfig for Complex Inputs
958	
959	Use `wandConfig` for fields that are hard to fill out manually:
960	- **Timestamps**: Use `generationType: 'timestamp'` to inject current date context into the AI prompt
961	- **JSON arrays**: Use `generationType: 'json-object'` for structured data
962	- **Complex queries**: Use a descriptive prompt explaining the expected format
963	
964	```typescript
965	{
966	  id: 'startTime',
967	  title: 'Start Time',
968	  type: 'short-input',
969	  mode: 'advanced',
970	  wandConfig: {
971	    enabled: true,
972	    prompt: 'Generate an ISO 8601 timestamp. Return ONLY the timestamp string.',
973	    generationType: 'timestamp',
974	  },
975	}
976	```
977	
978	### OAuth Scopes (Centralized System)
979	
980	Scopes are maintained in a single source of truth and reused everywhere:
981	
982	1. **Define scopes** in `lib/oauth/oauth.ts` under `OAUTH_PROVIDERS[provider].services[service].scopes`
983	2. **Add descriptions** in `SCOPE_DESCRIPTIONS` within `lib/oauth/utils.ts` for the OAuth modal UI
984	3. **Reference in auth.ts** using `getCanonicalScopesForProvider(providerId)` from `@/lib/oauth/utils`
985	4. **Reference in blocks** using `getScopesForService(serviceId)` from `@/lib/oauth/utils`
986	
987	**Never hardcode scope arrays** in `auth.ts` or block `requiredScopes`. Always import from the centralized source.
988	
989	```typescript
990	// In auth.ts (Better Auth config)
991	scopes: getCanonicalScopesForProvider('{service}'),
992	
993	// In block credential sub-block
994	requiredScopes: getScopesForService('{service}'),
995	```
996	
997	### Common Gotchas
998	
999	1. **OAuth serviceId must match** - The `serviceId` in oauth-input must match the OAuth provider configuration
1000	2. **All tool IDs MUST be snake_case** - `stripe_create_payment`, not `stripeCreatePayment`. This applies to tool `id` fields, registry keys, `tools.access` arrays, and `tools.config.tool` return values
1001	3. **Block type is snake_case** - `type: 'stripe'`, not `type: 'Stripe'`
1002	4. **Alphabetical ordering** - Keep imports and registry entries alphabetically sorted
1003	5. **Required can be conditional** - Use `required: { field: 'op', value: 'create' }` instead of always true
1004	6. **DependsOn clears options** - When a dependency changes, selector options are refetched
1005	7. **Never pass Buffer directly to fetch** - Convert to `new Uint8Array(buffer)` for TypeScript compatibility
1006	8. **Always handle legacy file params** - Keep hidden `fileContent` params for backwards compatibility
1007	9. **Optional fields use advanced mode** - Set `mode: 'advanced'` on rarely-used optional fields
1008	10. **Complex inputs need wandConfig** - Timestamps, JSON arrays, and other hard-to-type values should have `wandConfig` enabled
1009	11. **Never hardcode scopes** - Use `getScopesForService()` in blocks and `getCanonicalScopesForProvider()` in auth.ts
1010	12. **Always add scope descriptions** - New scopes must have entries in `SCOPE_DESCRIPTIONS` within `lib/oauth/utils.ts`
1011	13. **OAuth service IDs need deployment capabilities** - Every visible OAuth integration must resolve through `OAUTH_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES`; shared Google/Microsoft aliases map to their provider capability
1012	14. **Keep runtime and presentation separate** - Runtime OAuth fields live in `packages/deployment-config/src/env-capabilities.ts`; CLI input modes live in the exhaustively checked `packages/sim-setup/src/capability-config.ts` mapping
1013

1 --- 2 name: add-trigger 3 description: Create webhook or polling triggers for a Sim integration 4 argument-hint: 5 --- 6 7 # Add Trigger 8 9 You are an expert at creating webhook and polling triggers for Sim. You understand the trigger system, the generic `buildTriggerSubBlocks` helper, polling infrastructure, and how triggers connect to blocks. 10 11 ## Your Task 12 13 1. Research what webhook events the service supports — if the service lacks reliable webhooks, use polling 14 2. Create the trigger files using the generic builder (webhook) or manual config (polling) 15 3. Create a provider handler (webhook) or polling handler (polling) 16 4. Register triggers and connect them to the block 17 18 ## Hard Rule: No Guessed Webhook Payload Schemas 19 20 If the service docs do not clearly show the webhook payload JSON for an event, you MUST tell the user instead of guessing trigger outputs or `formatInput` mappings. 21 22 - Do NOT invent payload field names 23 - Do NOT guess nested event object paths 24 - Do NOT infer output fields from the UI or marketing docs 25 - Do NOT write `formatInput` against unverified webhook bodies 26 27 If the payload shape is unknown, do one of these instead: 28 1. Ask the user for sample webhook payloads 29 2. Ask the user for a test webhook source so you can inspect a real event 30 3. Implement only the event registration/setup portions whose payloads are documented 31 4. Leave the trigger unimplemented and explicitly say which payload fields are unknown 32 33 ## Directory Structure 34 35 ``` 36 apps/sim/triggers/{service}/ 37 ├── index.ts # Barrel exports 38 ├── utils.ts # Service-specific helpers (options, instructions, extra fields, outputs) 39 ├── {event_a}.ts # Primary trigger (includes dropdown) 40 ├── {event_b}.ts # Secondary trigger (no dropdown) 41 └── webhook.ts # Generic webhook trigger (optional, for "all events") 42 43 apps/sim/lib/webhooks/ 44 ├── provider-subscription-utils.ts # Shared subscription helpers (getProviderConfig, getNotificationUrl) 45 ├── providers/ 46 │ ├── {service}.ts # Provider handler (auth, formatInput, matchEvent, subscriptions) 47 │ ├── types.ts # WebhookProviderHandler interface 48 │ ├── utils.ts # Shared helpers (createHmacVerifier, verifyTokenAuth, skipByEventTypes) 49 │ └── registry.ts # Handler map + default handler 50 ``` 51 52 ## Step 1: Create `utils.ts` 53 54 This file contains all service-specific helpers used by triggers. 55 56 ```typescript 57 import type { SubBlockConfig } from '@/blocks/types' 58 import type { TriggerOutput } from '@/triggers/types' 59 60 export const {service}TriggerOptions = [ 61 { label: 'Event A', id: '{service}_event_a' }, 62 { label: 'Event B', id: '{service}_event_b' }, 63 ] 64 65 export function {service}SetupInstructions(eventType: string): string { 66 const instructions = [ 67 'Copy the Webhook URL above', 68 'Go to {Service} Settings > Webhooks', 69 `Select the ${eventType} event type`, 70 'Paste the webhook URL and save', 71 'Click "Save" above to activate your trigger', 72 ] 73 return instructions 74 .map((instruction, index) => 75 `
${index + 1}. ${instruction}
` 76 ) 77 .join('') 78 } 79 80 export function build{Service}ExtraFields(triggerId: string): SubBlockConfig[] { 81 return [ 82 { 83 id: 'projectId', 84 title: 'Project ID (Optional)', 85 type: 'short-input', 86 placeholder: 'Leave empty for all projects', 87 mode: 'trigger', 88 condition: { field: 'selectedTriggerId', value: triggerId }, 89 }, 90 ] 91 } 92 93 export function build{Service}Outputs(): Record { 94 return { 95 eventType: { type: 'string', description: 'The type of event' }, 96 resourceId: { type: 'string', description: 'ID of the affected resource' }, 97 resource: { 98 id: { type: 'string', description: 'Resource ID' }, 99 name: { type: 'string', description: 'Resource name' }, 100 }, 101 } 102 } 103 ``` 104 105 ## Step 2: Create Trigger Files 106 107 **Primary trigger** — MUST include `includeDropdown: true`: 108 109 ```typescript 110 import { {Service}Icon } from '@/components/icons' 111 import { buildTriggerSubBlocks } from '@/triggers' 112 import { build{Service}ExtraFields, build{Service}Outputs, {service}SetupInstructions, {service}TriggerOptions } from '@/triggers/{service}/utils' 113 import type { TriggerConfig } from '@/triggers/types' 114 115 export const {service}EventATrigger: TriggerConfig = { 116 id: '{service}_event_a', 117 name: '{Service} Event A', 118 provider: '{service}', 119 description: 'Trigger workflow when Event A occurs', 120 version: '1.0.0', 121 icon: {Service}Icon, 122 subBlocks: buildTriggerSubBlocks({ 123 triggerId: '{service}_event_a', 124 triggerOptions: {service}TriggerOptions, 125 includeDropdown: true, 126 setupInstructions: {service}SetupInstructions('Event A'), 127 extraFields: build{Service}ExtraFields('{service}_event_a'), 128 }), 129 outputs: build{Service}Outputs(), 130 webhook: { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }, 131 } 132 ``` 133 134 **Secondary triggers** — NO `includeDropdown` (it's already in the primary): 135 136 ```typescript 137 export const {service}EventBTrigger: TriggerConfig = { 138 // Same as above but: id: '{service}_event_b', no includeDropdown 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 ## Step 3: Register and Wire 143 144 ### `apps/sim/triggers/{service}/index.ts` 145 146 ```typescript 147 export { {service}EventATrigger } from './event_a' 148 export { {service}EventBTrigger } from './event_b' 149 ``` 150 151 ### `apps/sim/triggers/registry.ts` 152 153 ```typescript 154 import { {service}EventATrigger, {service}EventBTrigger } from '@/triggers/{service}' 155 156 export const TRIGGER_REGISTRY: TriggerRegistry = { 157 // ... existing ... 158 {service}_event_a: {service}EventATrigger, 159 {service}_event_b: {service}EventBTrigger, 160 } 161 ``` 162 163 ### Block file (`apps/sim/blocks/blocks/{service}.ts`) 164 165 Wire triggers into the block so the trigger UI appears and `generate-docs.ts` discovers them. Two changes are needed: 166 167 1. **Spread trigger subBlocks** at the end of the block's `subBlocks` array 168 2. **Add `triggers` property** after `outputs` with `enabled: true` and `available: [...]` 169 170 ```typescript 171 import { getTrigger } from '@/triggers' 172 173 export const {Service}Block: BlockConfig = { 174 // ... 175 subBlocks: [ 176 // Regular tool subBlocks first... 177 ...getTrigger('{service}_event_a').subBlocks, 178 ...getTrigger('{service}_event_b').subBlocks, 179 ], 180 // ... tools, inputs, outputs ... 181 triggers: { 182 enabled: true, 183 available: ['{service}_event_a', '{service}_event_b'], 184 }, 185 } 186 ``` 187 188 **Versioned blocks (V1 + V2):** Many integrations have a hidden V1 block and a visible V2 block. Where you add the trigger wiring depends on how V2 inherits from V1: 189 190 - **V2 uses `...V1Block` spread** (e.g., Google Calendar): Add trigger to V1 — V2 inherits both `subBlocks` and `triggers` automatically. 191 - **V2 defines its own `subBlocks`** (e.g., Google Sheets): Add trigger to V2 (the visible block). V1 is hidden and doesn't need it. 192 - **Single block, no V2** (e.g., Google Drive): Add trigger directly. 193 194 `generate-docs.ts` deduplicates by base type (first match wins). If V1 is processed first without triggers, the V2 triggers won't appear in `integrations.json`. Always verify by checking the output after running the script. 195 196 ## Provider Handler 197 198 All provider-specific webhook logic lives in a single handler file: `apps/sim/lib/webhooks/providers/{service}.ts`. 199 200 ### When to Create a Handler 201 202 | Behavior | Method | Examples | 203 |---|---|---| 204 | HMAC signature auth | `verifyAuth` via `createHmacVerifier` | Ashby, Jira, Linear, Typeform | 205 | Custom token auth | `verifyAuth` via `verifyTokenAuth` | Generic, Google Forms | 206 | Event filtering | `matchEvent` | GitHub, Jira, Attio, HubSpot | 207 | Idempotency dedup | `extractIdempotencyId` | Slack, Stripe, Linear, Jira | 208 | Custom input formatting | `formatInput` | Slack, Teams, Attio, Ashby | 209 | Auto webhook creation | `createSubscription` | Ashby, Grain, Calendly, Airtable | 210 | Auto webhook deletion | `deleteSubscription` | Ashby, Grain, Calendly, Airtable | 211 | Challenge/verification | `handleChallenge` | Slack, WhatsApp, Teams | 212 | Custom success response | `formatSuccessResponse` | Slack, Twilio Voice, Teams | 213 214 If none apply, you don't need a handler. The default handler provides bearer token auth. 215 216 ### Example Handler 217 218 ```typescript 219 import crypto from 'crypto' 220 import { createLogger } from '@sim/logger' 221 import { safeCompare } from '@/lib/core/security/encryption' 222 import type { EventMatchContext, FormatInputContext, FormatInputResult, WebhookProviderHandler } from '@/lib/webhooks/providers/types' 223 import { createHmacVerifier } from '@/lib/webhooks/providers/utils' 224 225 const logger = createLogger('WebhookProvider:{Service}') 226 227 function validate{Service}Signature(secret: string, signature: string, body: string): boolean { 228 if (!secret || !signature || !body) return false 229 const computed = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body, 'utf8').digest('hex') 230 return safeCompare(computed, signature) 231 } 232 233 export const {service}Handler: WebhookProviderHandler = { 234 verifyAuth: createHmacVerifier({ 235 configKey: 'webhookSecret', 236 headerName: 'X-{Service}-Signature', 237 validateFn: validate{Service}Signature, 238 providerLabel: '{Service}', 239 }), 240 241 async matchEvent({ body, requestId, providerConfig }: EventMatchContext) { 242 const triggerId = providerConfig.triggerId as string | undefined 243 if (triggerId && triggerId !== '{service}_webhook') { 244 const { is{Service}EventMatch } = await import('@/triggers/{service}/utils') 245 if (!is{Service}EventMatch(triggerId, body as Record)) return false 246 } 247 return true 248 }, 249 250 async formatInput({ body }: FormatInputContext): Promise { 251 const b = body as Record 252 return { 253 input: { 254 eventType: b.type, 255 resourceId: (b.data as Record)?.id || '', 256 resource: b.data, 257 }, 258 } 259 }, 260 261 extractIdempotencyId(body: unknown) { 262 const obj = body as Record 263 return obj.id && obj.type ? `${obj.type}:${obj.id}` : null 264 }, 265 } 266 ``` 267 268 ### Register the Handler 269 270 In `apps/sim/lib/webhooks/providers/registry.ts`: 271 272 ```typescript 273 import { {service}Handler } from '@/lib/webhooks/providers/{service}' 274 275 const PROVIDER_HANDLERS: Record = { 276 // ... existing (alphabetical) ... 277 {service}: {service}Handler, 278 } 279 ``` 280 281 ## Output Alignment (Critical) 282 283 There are two sources of truth that **MUST be aligned**: 284 285 1. **Trigger `outputs`** — schema defining what fields SHOULD be available (UI tag dropdown) 286 2. **`formatInput` on the handler** — implementation that transforms raw payload into actual data 287 288 If they differ: the tag dropdown shows fields that don't exist, or actual data has fields users can't discover. 289 290 **Rules for `formatInput`:** 291 - Return `{ input: { ... } }` where inner keys match trigger `outputs` exactly 292 - Return `{ input: ..., skip: { message: '...' } }` to skip execution 293 - No wrapper objects or duplication 294 - Use `null` for missing optional data 295 296 ## Automatic Webhook Registration 297 298 If the service API supports programmatic webhook creation, implement `createSubscription` and `deleteSubscription` on the handler. The orchestration layer calls these automatically — **no code touches `route.ts`, `provider-subscriptions.ts`, or `deploy.ts`**. 299 300 ```typescript 301 import { getNotificationUrl, getProviderConfig } from '@/lib/webhooks/provider-subscription-utils' 302 import type { DeleteSubscriptionContext, SubscriptionContext, SubscriptionResult } from '@/lib/webhooks/providers/types' 303 304 export const {service}Handler: WebhookProviderHandler = { 305 async createSubscription(ctx: SubscriptionContext): Promise { 306 const config = getProviderConfig(ctx.webhook) 307 const apiKey = config.apiKey as string 308 if (!apiKey) throw new Error('{Service} API Key is required.') 309 310 const res = await fetch('https://api.{service}.com/webhooks', { 311 method: 'POST', 312 headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, 313 body: JSON.stringify({ url: getNotificationUrl(ctx.webhook) }), 314 }) 315 316 if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`{Service} error: ${res.status}`) 317 const { id } = (await res.json()) as { id: string } 318 return { providerConfigUpdates: { externalId: id } } 319 }, 320 321 async deleteSubscription(ctx: DeleteSubscriptionContext): Promise { 322 const config = getProviderConfig(ctx.webhook) 323 const { apiKey, externalId } = config as { apiKey?: string; externalId?: string } 324 if (!apiKey || !externalId) return 325 await fetch(`https://api.{service}.com/webhooks/${externalId}`, { 326 method: 'DELETE', 327 headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` }, 328 }).catch(() => {}) 329 }, 330 } 331 ``` 332 333 **Key points:** 334 - Throw from `createSubscription` — orchestration rolls back the DB webhook 335 - Never throw from `deleteSubscription` — log non-fatally 336 - Return `{ providerConfigUpdates: { externalId } }` — orchestration merges into `providerConfig` 337 - Add `apiKey` field to `build{Service}ExtraFields` with `password: true` 338 339 ## Trigger Outputs Schema 340 341 Trigger outputs use the same schema as block outputs (NOT tool outputs). 342 343 **Supported:** `type` + `description` for leaf fields, nested objects for complex data. 344 **NOT supported:** `optional: true`, `items` (those are tool-output-only features). 345 346 ```typescript 347 export function buildOutputs(): Record { 348 return { 349 eventType: { type: 'string', description: 'Event type' }, 350 timestamp: { type: 'string', description: 'When it occurred' }, 351 payload: { type: 'json', description: 'Full event payload' }, 352 resource: { 353 id: { type: 'string', description: 'Resource ID' }, 354 name: { type: 'string', description: 'Resource name' }, 355 }, 356 } 357 } 358 ``` 359 360 ## Polling Triggers 361 362 Use polling when the service lacks reliable webhooks (e.g., Google Sheets, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Gmail, RSS, IMAP). Polling triggers do NOT use `buildTriggerSubBlocks` — they define subBlocks manually. 363 364 ### Directory Structure 365 366 ``` 367 apps/sim/triggers/{service}/ 368 ├── index.ts # Barrel export 369 └── poller.ts # TriggerConfig with polling: true 370 371 apps/sim/lib/webhooks/polling/ 372 └── {service}.ts # PollingProviderHandler implementation 373 ``` 374 375 ### Polling Handler (`apps/sim/lib/webhooks/polling/{service}.ts`) 376 377 ```typescript 378 import { pollingIdempotency } from '@/lib/core/idempotency/service' 379 import type { PollingProviderHandler, PollWebhookContext } from '@/lib/webhooks/polling/types' 380 import { markWebhookFailed, markWebhookSuccess, resolveOAuthCredential, updateWebhookProviderConfig } from '@/lib/webhooks/polling/utils' 381 import { processPolledWebhookEvent } from '@/lib/webhooks/processor' 382 383 export const {service}PollingHandler: PollingProviderHandler = { 384 provider: '{service}', 385 label: '{Service}', 386 387 async pollWebhook(ctx: PollWebhookContext): Promise<'success' | 'failure'> { 388 const { webhookData, workflowData, requestId, logger } = ctx 389 const webhookId = webhookData.id 390 391 try { 392 // For OAuth services: 393 const accessToken = await resolveOAuthCredential(webhookData, '{service}', requestId) 394 const config = webhookData.providerConfig as unknown as {Service}WebhookConfig 395 396 // First poll: seed state, emit nothing 397 if (!config.lastCheckedTimestamp) { 398 await updateWebhookProviderConfig(webhookId, { lastCheckedTimestamp: new Date().toISOString() }, logger) 399 await markWebhookSuccess(webhookId, logger) 400 return 'success' 401 } 402 403 // Fetch changes since last poll, process with idempotency 404 // ... 405 406 await markWebhookSuccess(webhookId, logger) 407 return 'success' 408 } catch (error) { 409 logger.error(`[${requestId}] Error processing {service} webhook ${webhookId}:`, error) 410 await markWebhookFailed(webhookId, logger) 411 return 'failure' 412 } 413 }, 414 } 415 ``` 416 417 **Key patterns:** 418 - First poll seeds state and emits nothing (avoids flooding with existing data) 419 - Use `pollingIdempotency.executeWithIdempotency(provider, key, callback)` for dedup 420 - Use `processPolledWebhookEvent(webhookData, workflowData, payload, requestId)` to fire the workflow 421 - Use `updateWebhookProviderConfig(webhookId, partialConfig, logger)` for read-merge-write on state 422 - Use the latest server-side timestamp from API responses (not wall clock) to avoid clock skew 423 424 `apps/sim/lib/webhooks/polling/google-calendar.ts` 474 475 ## Option Lists: `selectorKey` or `options`, never a per-block fetcher 476 477 A sub-block gets its choices from exactly one of two places. There is no third. 478 479 **`selectorKey` — every remote list.** Register the list in `hooks/selectors/providers//selectors.ts`, add its key to `SelectorKey`, and point the sub-block at it. 11	 * Deterministic JSON serialization with object keys sorted, so structurally
12	 * identical payloads produce identical output regardless of key order.

14	function stableSerialize(value: unknown): string {
15	  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
16	    return `[${value.map((item) => stableSerialize(item)).join(',')}]`
17	  }
18	
19	  if (value && typeof value === 'object') {
20	    return `{${Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)
21	      .sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))
22	      .map(([key, nested]) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${stableSerialize(nested)}`)
23	      .join(',')}}`

57	  configKey,
58	  headerName,
59	  validateFn,
60	  providerLabel,
61	  requireSecret = false,
62	}: HmacVerifierOptions) {
63	  return async ({
64	    request,
65	    rawBody,
66	    requestId,
67	    providerConfig,
68	  }: AuthContext): Promise<NextResponse | null> => {
69	    const secret = providerConfig[configKey] as string | undefined
70	    if (!secret) {
71	      if (requireSecret) {
72	        logger.warn(`[${requestId}] ${providerLabel} webhook secret not configured`)
73	        return new NextResponse(`Unauthorized - Missing ${providerLabel} webhook secret`, {
74	          status: 401,
75	        })
76	      }

81	    if (!signature) {
82	      logger.warn(`[${requestId}] ${providerLabel} webhook missing signature header`)
83	      return new NextResponse(`Unauthorized - Missing ${providerLabel} signature`, { status: 401 })
84	    }

result.output:
### Trigger cards

A card in trigger mode paints its own sentence, from `canvasPresentation.triggerSentences`:

```ts
triggerSentences?: {
  default?: CanvasSentence
  byTrigger?: Record<string, CanvasSentence>   // keyed by trigger id
}
```

**Most blocks declare nothing.** Trigger mode usually exposes a webhook URL and a
signing secret — plumbing, not meaning — and the thing worth reading is *which*
event was picked. That is already curated as the trigger's `name` in
`apps/sim/triggers/`, so the card derives `Run on Pull Request Opened` with no
authoring at all. Declare `triggerSentences` only when the configuration is
itself the meaning, as Schedule's frequency is.

What the sentence *says* shifts with the mode, though the voice does not. An
action sentence names what the block does; a trigger sentence names what starts
the run — `Run on an email arriving in ⟨INBOX⟩`, never `Read an email`. It is a
separate slot rather than another `byOperation` key because trigger mode swaps
the subblock set wholesale, and the operation dropdown still holds its
action-mode default.

Sim's own entry points (`start_trigger`, `manual_trigger`, `chat_trigger`,
`api_trigger`, `input_trigger`, `starter`) are exempt: they *are* the start of
the run and their header already says so, so a sentence would only repeat it.

### Voice

- **Imperative, the card naming its own action.** `Post a message to ⟨#eng⟩`. Never
  `Posts a message` (third person), never `Post a Slack message` — the header
  already says Slack, so naming it again wastes the line. The heading above the
  sentence is the operation title (`Send Email`), and the two share a voice.
  `check:canvas-sentences` enforces this on action *and* trigger cards.
- **The sentence carries the verb.** It replaces the chips row, which is what
  shows the operation today. `List channels`, not `Channels`.
- **Lead with the verb, put the value last** where possible — the chip is the part
  a user scans for.
- **One clause per fact, most important first.** The card is 250px wide and
  wraps at ~2 lines; later clauses are the ones that fall off.
- **At most three value chips**, and two reads best — every chip adds width and
  pushes the card taller. An operation with no field worth showing is just a
  literal: `['List all channels']` is a complete, valid sentence.
- Sentence case, no trailing period, no articles you can drop (`Read schema of`
  beats `Read the schema of the table`).

### Structure

- **Mark the clauses the sentence is *about* `core`**, and leave the rest optional.
  A sentence may have as many core clauses as it needs to read whole — they hold
  only their own slot, so there is no one-anchor limit.
- **Use literal copy when every field is an optional filter.** A list/search
  operation whose filters are all optional has nothing worth a placeholder. Lead
  with a literal and let every clause be optional:
  `['List issues', { text: ', assigned to', field: 'assignee' }]`.
- **Each optional clause owns its leading connective.** Write
  `{ text: ', where', field: 'filter' }`, never
  `{ ..., after: ', where' }, { field: 'filter' }` — a dropped clause takes its own
  `text` with it, but an `after` on the *previous* clause survives and dangles.
- **Bare strings are always-on literal copy.** Prefer folding them into a clause's
  `text` so they can drop with the value.
- **A chip is a noun, never the verb.** A chip renders a dropdown's *label*, so
  when those labels are themselves verbs (`Archive` / `Unarchive`) you cannot
  build the sentence around one — `Apply ⟨Archive⟩ to thread ⟨id⟩` is the
  result. State the change instead: `Set thread ⟨id⟩ to ⟨Archive⟩`.

### The four mistakes that break cards silently

1. **Naming one member of a canonical pair.** A `canonicalParamId` group has a
   basic picker and an advanced raw-id input; an advanced-mode user has only the
   second filled. List every member:
   `field: ['tableSelector', 'manualTableId']`. Three naming conventions are in
   use (`xSelector`/`x`, `xSelector`/`manualX`, `uploadX`/`xRef`), so take the
   membership from the spec's `canonicalGroups` — you cannot derive it from the
   canonical id.

   A `field` array is also the right tool for **mutually exclusive alternates
   that are not a canonical pair** — Slack's destination is a channel *or* a DM
   id, Sendblue's is a number list *or* a group id. First available wins.
2. **Referencing a field the operation never shows.** A subblock gated
   `condition: { field: 'operation', value: [...] }` can only appear in the
   `byOperation` entries it lists.
3. **Two operations that render the same prose.** On a block with dozens of
   similar read endpoints it is easy to paste a clause and never adjust it, so
   `get_thread` and `get_thread_replies` both say `Read thread ⟨id⟩` and the
   card cannot tell the user which one runs. Name what each actually returns.

   The check runs on **both** readings, so two operations may not collide once
   their optional clauses are empty either — which is how an untouched card
   reads. `Add tag ⟨id⟩ to contact ⟨x⟩` and `… to conversation ⟨y⟩` both bare
   to `Add tag ⟨id⟩`; marking the target clause `core` is what tells them apart.
4. **An optional clause carrying the action's target or scope.** This one the
   validator cannot catch — 895 clauses fleet-wide fit the shape and only ~45
   are defects, so the discriminator is semantic. Ask what the sentence means
   with that clause gone. `Remove user ⟨id⟩` reads as deleting the user, not
   removing them from a group; `Delete records from ⟨index⟩` reads as clearing
   the whole index. If the truncated reading names a broader or different
   action, mark that clause `core` so it holds its place. `Delete thread ⟨id⟩`
   losing an optional `, in ⟨channel⟩` is fine — it still means the same thing.

### Two rules the validator enforces on your copy

- **No article in front of a chip.** For a `core` chip the noun already supplies
  one, so `Create a ⟨campaignType⟩` reads `Create a a campaign type` — drop the
  article and let the noun carry it. For an optional chip the article has to agree
  with a dropdown *label* whose initial sound you cannot know
  (`Create a ⟨A/B Split⟩ campaign`), so move the value out from behind it:
  `Create a campaign of type ⟨type⟩`.
- **Both halves of a correlative, or neither.** A clause opening `from …` or
  `between …` needs the clause carrying `to …`/`and …` to survive an empty card,
  or `Route from ⟨an origin⟩` describes a different journey. Mark both halves
  `core`.

### Versioned blocks

28 files export a `_v2` (or `_v3`…) variant that spreads the base — `export const
GmailV2Block = { ...GmailBlock, type: 'gmail_v2', ... }`. The spread carries
`canvasPresentation` with it, which is right only when the variant has the *same*
operation dropdown.

**When the operation sets differ, inheritance is a bug.** `file.ts` chains
`FileV5 → FileV4 → FileV3`, and an inherited `byOperation` carries keys like
`file_parser_v3` that later dropdowns do not have — the validator reports
`no option with id`. Give every export whose dropdown differs its own
`canvasPresentation`.

Always run `--block=<type>` for *every* registry type the file exports, not just
the base. That is what tells you which case you are in.

/**
 * Validates that every `<path d='…'>` in `apps/sim/components/icons.tsx` is
 * syntactically well-formed SVG path data.
 *
 * Malformed path data does not crash the build or fail TypeScript — the browser
 * silently drops the bad segment and logs `<path> attribute d: Expected number`
 * / `Expected arc flag` to the console. A bulk icon reformat once corrupted
 * several brand icons this way (dropped arc-flag digits, mangled cubic operands
 * like `c00,00,00`), flooding the integrations page with dozens of console
 * errors that no existing check caught. This script is that missing gate.
 *
 * It walks each `d` string against the SVG path grammar and fails if any
 * command has the wrong operand count or an arc flag that is not `0`/`1`.
 * Number scanning handles the compact forms the spec allows (packed decimals
 * `.5.5`, sign-delimited `1-2`, exponents, and arc flags packed against
 * neighbours like `001.39`), so valid minified paths pass unflagged.
 *
 * Run: `bun run scripts/check-icon-paths.ts`
 */

import path from 'node:path'

  l: 2,
  h: 1,
  v: 1,
  c: 6,
  s: 4,
  q: 4,
  t: 2,
  a: 7,
  z: 0,
}

const isWsp = (ch: string) => ch === ' ' || ch === '\t' || ch === '\n' || ch === '\r' || ch === '\f'

import { BlockInfoCard } from "@/components/ui/block-info-card"

## Usage Instructions

Send iMessages from a Photon-managed number and trigger workflows on inbound messages. Photon runs the iMessage line, so no Mac is required. Reply into an existing conversation with the chat ID from the trigger, or start one from a phone number or Apple ID email.



## Actions

### Send iMessage

Send an iMessage to a phone number or email address, or reply into an existing chat, through a Photon project

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `projectId` | string | Yes | Photon project ID from app.photon.codes |
| `projectSecret` | string | Yes | Photon project secret from app.photon.codes |
| `to` | string | No | Recipient phone number in E.164 form \(e.g. +14155551234\) or an Apple ID email. Starts or reuses a direct conversation. Omit when using chatId. |
| `chatId` | string | No | Existing chat GUID to send into, such as the chatId from an iMessage trigger. Required to reach a group chat. Omit when using to. |
| `text` | string | Yes | Message text to send. iMessage is plain text, so Markdown is not rendered. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `messageId` | string | Identifier of the sent message |
| `chatId` | string | Chat GUID the message was sent to. Pass this back to reply into the same chat. |
| `timestamp` | string | ISO 8601 time the message was sent |



## Triggers

A **Trigger** is a block that starts a workflow when an event happens in this service.

### Photon iMessage Received

Trigger workflow when an inbound iMessage is received through Photon

#### Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `webhookSecret` | string | Yes | Signing secret from the Photon webhook, used to verify the X-Spectrum-Signature header on every delivery. |

---
title: "Sim"
description: "Connect a Sim workflow to iMessage through Photon"
---

[Sim](https://sim.ai) builds AI agents as visual workflows. The **iMessage (Photon)**
integration puts one of those workflows on iMessage: an inbound message starts a
workflow run, and the workflow sends its answer back as an iMessage. Photon runs
the iMessage line, so no Mac stays online.

You configure both halves in Sim — there is no `spectrum-ts` code to write. This
guide covers the Photon side: provisioning, credentials, and webhook
verification. The block's fields are documented in the
[Sim integration reference](https://docs.sim.ai/integrations/photon_imessage).

## What you need

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create a Photon project">
    In the [Photon dashboard](https://app.photon.codes), create a project and
    register the phone number the agent will message from. Copy the **project
    ID** and **project secret**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add the block in Sim">
    In your Sim workflow, add the **iMessage (Photon)** block and paste the
    project ID and secret. That is enough to send.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add the trigger">
    Switch the block to trigger mode and pick **Photon iMessage Received**. Copy
    the webhook URL Sim shows you.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Register the webhook">
    Back in the Photon dashboard, create a webhook pointing at that URL (public
    HTTPS only). Copy the **signing secret** — it is shown once — and paste it
    into the trigger's *Webhook Signing Secret* field.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
  The project secret and the webhook signing secret are different credentials.
  The project secret authorizes Photon API access; the signing secret
  authenticates inbound deliveries. Keep both out of source control.
</Warning>

## How deliveries are verified

Photon signs every delivery, and Sim rejects anything that fails the check —
including a delivery with no signing secret configured, since an inbound message
can drive an agent.

The scheme is the one described in [Webhooks](/spectrum-ts/webhooks):
`X-Spectrum-Signature: v0=<hex>` carries `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "v0:" + timestamp
+ ":" + rawBody)`, checked against `X-Spectrum-Timestamp` within a five-minute
replay window. Sim verifies it with `verifySpectrumSignature` from
[`@spectrum-ts/core/webhook`](/spectrum-ts/webhooks), so the check stays in step
with the platform.

Deliveries are at-least-once. Sim deduplicates runs on the message ID, so a
retried delivery does not re-run the workflow.

## Replying into the same conversation

The trigger emits a `chatId` — the conversation's chat GUID. Pass it to the send
block's **Chat ID** field to reply into the same thread. Sending to a **Recipient**
instead (a phone number or Apple ID email) starts or reuses a direct
conversation.

A group chat can only be reached by `chatId`, and only one the workflow has
already received a message from: Photon has no by-id resolver for a group it has
not seen.

## What the trigger gives you

Each run receives the message plus its context: `text`, `contentType`,
`senderId`, `chatId`, `chatType`, `timestamp`, `attachments`, and the full `raw`
payload. A reply's text is read through to its inner content, and a grouped
message (text plus media) surfaces its text and its attachment metadata
together.

Attachment **bytes** are not delivered by webhook — only metadata. See
[Fetching attachments](/spectrum-ts/providers/imessage/messaging-features/fetching-attachments)
for reading the bytes through the platform.

## Limitations

- **Plain text.** iMessage does not render Markdown; formatting is sent as
  literal characters.
- **No token streaming.** A workflow's answer arrives as one complete message.
- **Read receipts and typing are not triggers.** They arrive on the same stream
  but do not start a workflow run, so a conversation is not re-run on every
  signal.

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Sim integration reference" icon="book" href="https://docs.sim.ai/integrations/photon_imessage">
    Field-by-field reference for the block and its trigger.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Webhooks" icon="webhook" href="/spectrum-ts/webhooks">
    The signature scheme and delivery semantics behind the trigger.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

Both repos are clean and committed. The integration is built and passing every check — but I stopped short of pushing or opening the PR, for one reason you need to resolve.

## What exists now

**`~/Documents/Projects/sim`** (your fork, branch `feat/photon-imessage-integration`, one commit off `upstream/staging`) — a complete **iMessage (Photon)** integration for Sim's catalog:

- **Send tool** (`photon_imessage_send_message`) → an internal Next.js route, because Photon reaches iMessage over gRPC and can't be a plain fetch from the tool layer. Spectrum instances are cached per project and evicted LRU, since constructing one mints cloud credentials and opens a connection per line.
- **Trigger** (`photon_imessage_message_received`) with a webhook handler that verifies signatures using Photon's own `verifySpectrumSignature` from `@spectrum-ts/core/webhook` — the portable entry your last release added is exactly right for this. It fails **closed** when no secret is configured (Sim's shared `createHmacVerifier` fails open, which I judged wrong for a trigger that drives an agent), and dedupes on message ID since delivery is at-least-once.
- Block, icon, and all six registries wired; docs page generated.

I took the payload mapping from `slimEnvelopeSchema` in your repo rather than inferring it — Sim's contribution guide explicitly forbids guessed webhook schemas, and one test asserts `formatInput`'s keys match the trigger outputs exactly, since nothing type-checks that link and drift silently empties the tag dropdown.

**Verification:** `tsc` clean, lint clean, 20 new tests pass, and 651 tests across 47 related files pass with no regressions. `integration-catalog:check`, `deployment-config:check`, `docs:check`, `check:canvas-sentences`, `check:trigger-block-cycle`, and all three icon validators pass.

**`~/Documents/Projects/spectrum-ts`** (branch `docs/sim-integration`) — a `docs/integrations/sim.mdx.vel` guide alongside eve and Chat SDK, plus the nav entry.

## Why I didn't submit

**The icon is a placeholder I drew** — a message bubble with a spark, monochrome and theme-safe, but not Photon's actual brand mark. Sim's own integration guide says to get the real SVG from the service rather than inventing one, and I'd be putting a fabricated logo into a public catalog under the Photon name. Paste me the real SVG and I'll swap it in; it's a contained change to `PhotonIcon` in `apps/sim/components/icons.tsx` (the docs copy regenerates).

Two smaller things worth knowing:

- **Commits are unsigned.** Your git config has `commit.gpgsign=true` via 1Password SSH, which needs an interactive approval I can't give. Re-sign with `git commit --amend -S --no-edit` on each branch.
- **No end-to-end run against a real Photon project.** The signature path is verified by real HMAC round-trips in tests, but I have no credentials, so nothing has actually sent an iMessage or received a live delivery. Worth one real send before submitting.

Scope I deliberately kept to v1: text send plus message-received. Reactions, typing, and attachment sending are natural follow-ups. Group chats are reachable only via `chatId` from a trigger, since Photon has no by-id resolver for an unseen group — that's an upstream constraint, and it's documented in both the block description and the guide.
